KRAB_ZNF.name: KRAB zinc-finger proteins (KZFPs)
KRAB_ZNF.short: KRAB zinc-finger proteins (KZFPs) are the largest family of DNA-binding proteins in the human genome: roughly 350 to 380 genes, most named only ZNF followed by a number. Each combines a KRAB repression domain, which recruits the corepressor TRIM28/KAP1 and the histone methyltransferase SETDB1, with a tandem array of C2H2 zinc fingers that reads a long, protein-specific stretch of DNA. Most of those stretches lie inside transposable elements, and the family has expanded and diversified alongside successive waves of element invasion. This atlas entry is therefore a bucket, not a motif: its 587 matrices come from 304 different proteins, run from 4 to 38 bp, and mostly do not resemble one another. A hit identifies one protein's site, not a family motif.

HD_Q50.name: Q50 homeodomain (DLX/MSX/LHX-type, TAATTA)
HD_Q50.short: About half of the roughly 200 human homeodomain proteins carry glutamine at position 50 of the domain and read the palindromic hexamer TAATTA. This family gathers 275 published motifs for 89 gene symbols: DLX1-6, MSX1-3, the LIM-homeodomain proteins LHX1-9 and ISL1/2, ALX1/3/4, ARX, PRRX1/2, EMX, EN, GBX, BARHL, LMX, SHOX, VAX and TLX, plus the paired-like factors VSX1/2, RAX/RAX2, PHOX2A/2B, NOBOX, MIXL1, VENTX, PROP1, DRGX, BSX, OTP and SEBOX and, from another family again, PDX1. Grouping follows the specificity a protein actually has rather than its gene family. Many of these proteins also bind cooperatively as dimers on TAATNNNATTA palindromes, which is where most real discrimination lies; a single TAATTA match carries almost no information.

ZNF_UNNAMED.name: Unnamed zinc-finger archetypes
ZNF_UNNAMED.short: Not a motif but a label gap. The Vierstra footprint atlas groups redundant matrices from several databases into archetypes, each named after the factor groups whose motifs clustered into it. For 256 of the 693 archetypes in this atlas that name collapses to a generic token, ZNF, ZFP, ZBTB, ZSCAN or ZKSCAN, so the only claim being made is that some C2H2 zinc finger binds here. These 256 matrices are long, high-information and almost entirely unrelated to one another: not one has a close match to another member of this entry. A hit means you matched a specific, reproducible zinc-finger matrix whose protein was never named, and the useful next step is to find that matrix's nearest named neighbour.

ZNF_OTHER.name: Other C2H2 zinc fingers
ZNF_OTHER.short: The remainder of the C2H2 zinc-finger class: factors that are neither KRAB zinc-finger proteins nor members of a family with its own entry. Ninety-six named genes appear here, from well-studied cases such as ZNF335, ZNF341, ZFAT and ZFTA to dozens of ZNF numbers with almost no literature. What they share is the fold, and little else: the 168 matrices in this entry are mutually unrelated, with a cohesion of 0.38 and a median length of 12 bp. The evidence behind them is nonetheless much better than for the KRAB group, with 39 of 93 HOCOMOCO models at the top grade and many supported in vitro. A hit here identifies one named protein at best, never a family motif.

RXR_HETERO.name: RXR and its heterodimers
RXR_HETERO.short: This family covers retinoid X receptors (RXRA/B/G) and the receptors that heterodimerize with them: retinoic acid receptors (RARA/B/G), thyroid hormone receptors (THRA/THRB), the vitamin D receptor (VDR), the PPARs, the liver X receptors (NR1H2/NR1H3), FXR (NR1H4) and the xenobiotic sensors PXR and CAR (NR1I2/NR1I3). Every member reads the same hexameric half-site, AGGTCA (more precisely RGKTCA), so the half-site sequence tells you nothing about which receptor bound. What does carry information is how two half-sites are arranged: direct repeats separated by 1 to 5 bp (DR1 through DR5), inverted repeats and everted repeats. Spacing and orientation, not half-site identity, are the readable signal here.

FOX.name: Forkhead (FOX)
FOX.short: Forkhead box (FOX) proteins are a family of about 50 human transcription factors that bind DNA as monomers through a ~100-residue winged-helix domain, named for the two loops, or wings, that flank its three-helix core. Nearly all of them read the same seven-base element, RYAAAYA, usually written GTAAACA or, on the opposite strand, TGTTTAC. The family includes the FOXA pioneer factors that engage nucleosomal DNA and open liver, prostate and breast enhancers; the insulin- and stress-controlled FOXO proteins; FOXC, FOXE, FOXG and FOXL factors needed for eye, thyroid, forebrain and ovary development; and the proliferation factor FOXM1. Because the DNA-contacting residues are almost invariant across the family, a forkhead match tells you that a FOX protein could bind there, but rarely which one.

KLF_SP.name: KLF / SP (GC-box)
KLF_SP.short: The SP and KLF proteins are about 26 human transcription factors that each use three C2H2 zinc fingers to read a nine- to ten-base GC-rich element. Two classical forms of that element exist: the GC-box GGGGCGGGG, found in the SV40 21-bp repeats and in most CpG-island promoters, and the CACCC-box CCACACCC of erythroid promoters such as beta-globin. In vitro selection puts the family consensus at CCACGCCC, which is the same site read from the other strand. Because all 26 proteins share the same finger code, sequence alone cannot say which one is bound; a GC-box hit identifies the family and, given how common GC-rich sequence is in promoters, often identifies very little else.

SOX.name: SOX (HMG box)
SOX.short: SOX proteins are the 20 human transcription factors built around a single SRY-type HMG box, a 78-residue L-shaped domain that binds DNA entirely in the minor groove, wedges a hydrophobic residue between base pairs and bends the double helix by 70-80 degrees. They read a six- to seven-base core usually written AACAAT, or CATTGTT/ATTGTT on the opposite strand. A SOX protein bound alone does little; transcriptional output comes from a partner factor on an adjacent site, most famously OCT4 in the SOX-OCT composite element of pluripotency enhancers, and from dimeric palindromic sites used by SOX8, SOX9 and SOX10. The family covers sex determination (SRY, SOX9), cartilage (SOX9, SOX5, SOX6), neural stem cells (SOX2), neural crest and melanocytes (SOX10) and endothelium (SOX17, SOX18).

NEUROD_ATOH.name: NeuroD / Atonal / ASCL
NEUROD_ATOH.short: Class II basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) proteins of the Atonal, achaete-scute, Olig and NSCL groups — NEUROD1/2, NEUROG1-3, ATOH1/7/8, ASCL1/2, OLIG1-3, PTF1A, BHLHA15, FIGLA, MSGN1, NHLH1/2 and relatives — bind DNA only as heterodimers with the broadly expressed class I E-proteins TCF3, TCF4 and TCF12. The dimer reads a six-base E-box, CANNTG; this group prefers CAGATG (CATCTG on the opposite strand), with CATATG and CAGCTG as the two common variants. These factors are commitment switches for progenitors in the nervous system, inner ear, retina, pancreas, intestine and presomitic mesoderm, and several of them — ASCL1, NEUROD1, NEUROG2, ATOH1 — are the active ingredients of direct reprogramming protocols that convert fibroblasts into neurons.

HD_POU.name: POU (octamer)
HD_POU.short: The octamer ATGCAAAT is the site read by the 16 human POU-domain factors, including OCT1/POU2F1, OCT2/POU2F2, PIT1/POU1F1, the BRN2/BRN1 group (POU3F1-4), the BRN3 group (POU4F1-3) and OCT4/POU5F1. What makes the family unusual is the binding unit: a POU-specific domain and a homeodomain joined by a flexible linker, so the two halves of the site can be re-arranged. The same proteins therefore also form dimers on the PORE and MORE elements and sit next to SOX partners in the SOX-OCT composite elements that control pluripotency genes. Hits matter because octamer elements drive immunoglobulin and snRNA promoters and because OCT4 occupancy of SOX-OCT sites is a defining feature of pluripotent cells. The motif is short and AT-rich, so it is common.

ETS_CLASS1.name: ETS class I (ETS1/ERG/FLI1)
ETS_CLASS1.short: ETS proteins are a family of 28 human transcription factors that each bind DNA through a single ~85-residue winged helix-turn-helix domain and read a nine-base site whose informative part is the four-base core GGA(A/T). The class I members - ETS1 and ETS2, ERG, FLI1, FEV, the PEA3 proteins ETV1/4/5, the ternary complex factors ELK1/3/4, the repressors ERF and ETV3, and GABPA - select essentially the same sequence, ACCGGAAGT, so a match names the class rather than a protein. These sites sit just upstream of a large fraction of human promoters and, in enhancers, next to RUNX, GATA, PAX and SRF sites. Class I also contains every ETS gene recurrently rearranged in cancer: ERG in prostate cancer, FLI1 and ERG in Ewing sarcoma, ETV1 and ETV4 in both.

AP1.name: AP-1 (FOS/JUN)
AP1.short: AP-1 is the collective name for dimers of the JUN proteins (JUN, JUNB, JUND) with the FOS proteins (FOS, FOSB, FOSL1, FOSL2), together with the related basic region-leucine zipper partners ATF3, JDP2 and BATF/BATF2/BATF3. They bind the seven-base TPA response element TGA(C/G)TCA, two TGAC half-sites read one per subunit, and also the one-base-longer cyclic-AMP response element TGACGTCA. FOS and JUN were among the first proto-oncogenes described, and AP-1 activity rises within minutes of growth-factor, cytokine, ultraviolet or oxidative stimulation. The site is one of the most frequently occupied sequences in accessible chromatin, concentrated in distal enhancers, where AP-1 binding helps keep regions open for other factors. Because every member reads the same seven bases, a match names the family rather than the protein.

HD_HOX_ANT.name: Anterior HOX (HOX1-8)
HD_HOX_ANT.short: The 39 human HOX genes sit in four clusters and specify position along the head-to-tail axis. This family covers paralogue groups 1 to 8 - the anterior and central HOX proteins - with 75 motifs for 27 gene symbols. Their homeodomains read the generic TAAT core, written TAATTA for groups 1-3 and shifting to TAATGA or TAATGG for groups 4-8. On their own these proteins are essentially interchangeable in vitro: no matrix separates HOXA5 from HOXB5 or HOXC6. Real sequence discrimination appears only in complex with the TALE cofactors PBX and MEIS, which build a bipartite site, ATGATTNATNN, whose HOX half-site shifts stepwise along the cluster.

HD_HOX_POST.name: Posterior HOX (HOX9-13, AbdB-like)
HD_HOX_POST.short: HOX paralogue groups 9 to 13 - the Abdominal-B-like or posterior HOX proteins - read a different core from the rest of the homeodomain superfamily. Where most homeodomains require TAAT, these prefer TTAT, and their in vitro sites extend to TTTTACGAC (equivalently GTCGTAAAA on the opposite strand). This family collects 63 motifs for the 16 posterior HOX genes: HOXA9-A13, HOXB9, HOXB13, HOXC9-C13 and HOXD9-D13. The longer, AT-rich site makes these motifs considerably rarer and more informative than a bare TAAT hit, but the 16 paralogues remain indistinguishable from each other. Groups 9-10 partner with PBX, groups 11-13 with MEIS instead.

HD_TALE.name: TALE homeodomain (PBX/MEIS/TGIF)
HD_TALE.short: TALE homeodomain factors - PBX1-4, MEIS1-3, PKNOX1/2 (PREP1/2) and TGIF1/2 with the TGIF2LX/TGIF2LY retrogenes - carry a homeodomain with three extra residues inserted between helices 1 and 2, the Three Amino acid Loop Extension that names the class. That insertion creates a pocket that docks the hexapeptide of HOX proteins, which is how these factors turn otherwise generic HOX binding into specific composite sites. Two cores dominate the family: MEIS, PKNOX and TGIF read TGACAG, usually as the palindrome TGACAGCTGTCA, while PBX proteins read TGAT and assemble PBX-HOX elements (TGATTNAT) and PBX-MEIS elements (TGATTGACAG). These composite sites are the reason HOX and TALE factors have any DNA-level specificity at all.

TBX.name: T-box
TBX.short: T-box sites are read by the seventeen human T-box proteins - TBXT (Brachyury), TBX1 to TBX6, TBX10, TBX15, TBX18 to TBX22, TBR1, EOMES and MGA - through a ~180-residue T domain that inserts a helix deep into a widened minor groove, a recognition mode found in no other family. The unit of binding is an eight-base half-site, AGGTGTGA, written TCACACCT in the other orientation. Brachyury binds a palindromic pair of half-sites as a dimer; several paralogues occupy single half-sites or tandem repeats instead. These factors specify the notochord, heart, limbs, pharyngeal apparatus and T-helper-1 lineage, and mutations in individual genes cause distinct human malformation syndromes - but the paralogues are essentially indistinguishable from sequence.

ZBTB_OTHER.name: Other BTB-ZF (ZBTB)
ZBTB_OTHER.short: BTB-ZF proteins, also called POZ-ZF, pair an N-terminal BTB/POZ domain, a dimerization module, with a short C2H2 zinc-finger array. This entry collects the 28 less-studied members: ZBTB1 to ZBTB6, ZBTB8A and ZBTB8B, ZBTB11, 12, 14, 16, 20, 22, 24, 26, 32, 37, 40 to 45, 47 and 49, plus myoneurin (MYNN) and ZNF131. The distinctive BTB-ZFs with well-mapped sites, among them BCL6, HIC1/2, ZBTB7A/B, MIZ1, ZBTB18, Kaiso and TZAP, are split into their own entries. It is not a single motif: 60 matrices, cohesion 0.42, median length 10 bp. Several members do read inverted-repeat sites, as obligate dimerization predicts, but the half-sites differ from protein to protein.

HD_NKX.name: NKX
HD_NKX.short: NKX proteins are homeodomain transcription factors related to Drosophila tinman and vnd, and they are the main exception to the rule that homeodomains read a TAAT core. NKX2-1 (TTF-1), NKX2-2 to NKX2-8, NKX3-1 and NKX3-2 prefer TAAGTG (read as CACTTA on the other strand), a specificity recognized as unusual when TTF-1 was first cloned. The family collects 51 motifs for 16 genes, including NKX1-1/1-2, NKX6-1 to NKX6-3 and NANOG. It is the least cohesive homeodomain family in this atlas because the NKX6 proteins in fact read a conventional TAAT core rather than TAAGTG, so the label covers two different sites.

HD_PAIRED.name: PAX paired domain
HD_PAIRED.short: The paired domain is a bipartite DNA-binding domain, unique to the nine human PAX proteins, that reads an unusually long site: a GTCACGC(A/T)TGA core set inside a footprint of roughly 15 to 20 base pairs. Two helix-turn-helix subdomains, PAI and RED, grip adjacent stretches of the double helix, so the recognition surface is far larger than that of a single homeodomain. PAX3, PAX4, PAX6 and PAX7 additionally carry a complete homeodomain that contributes an independent TAAT half site, making their composite elements longer still. PAX sites are therefore among the most information-rich transcription factor motifs in the genome. These factors specify the eye, thyroid, kidney, pancreatic beta cells, B lymphocytes and muscle progenitors, and paired-domain mutations cause aniridia, Waardenburg syndrome and renal-coloboma syndrome.

ZSCAN.name: SCAN-domain zinc fingers (ZSCAN/ZKSCAN)
ZSCAN.short: The larger, thinner-documented half of the human SCAN-domain zinc fingers: 26 labels including ZSCAN1, 2, 5, 9, 12, 16, 23, 25, 26, 30 and 31, ZKSCAN2, 4, 5, 7 and 8, and the older names ZNF165, ZNF174, ZNF232, ZNF396, ZNF444 and ZNF449. Each combines an N-terminal SCAN domain, an approximately 80-residue leucine-rich module that dimerizes, with a tandem C2H2 finger array; the ZKSCAN members also carry a KRAB domain. This is not a single motif. The 48 matrices here form roughly twenty per-protein groups that do not resemble one another, ranging from ZSCAN16's TGTTAACAGAGCCTC to ZNF444's poly-C run. Functional data exist for only a handful of members.

IRF.name: IRF
IRF.short: The nine human interferon regulatory factors, IRF1 through IRF9, bind DNA with an N-terminal winged helix-turn-helix domain studded with five conserved tryptophans. Each domain reads only a short AANTGAAA half-site, so functional elements are tandem repeats of it: the interferon-stimulated response element (ISRE), written RNGAAANNGAAACT or, on the other strand, AGTTTCNNTTTC. The same half-site also appears in two named composites - the EICE with PU.1 or SPIB, and the AICE with BATF-JUN - which is how IRF4 and IRF8, weak DNA binders on their own, reach their targets. IRFs drive the type I and type II interferon responses, myeloid and lymphoid development, and plasma cell differentiation; IRF6 is the non-immune outlier, acting in epithelium, where mutations cause orofacial clefting.

E2F.name: E2F / DP
E2F.short: E2F factors are the transcriptional output of the retinoblastoma (RB) pathway and set the G1/S transition. Eight human genes, E2F1-E2F8, encode a winged-helix DNA-binding domain. E2F1-E2F6 bind DNA only as heterodimers with a DP subunit (TFDP1 or TFDP2); E2F7 and E2F8 carry two tandem winged-helix domains and work without DP. All of them read essentially the same GC-rich eight-base element, written TTTSSCGC and just as often rendered on the other strand as GCGGGAAA. E2F1-E2F3 are activators released when CDKs phosphorylate RB; E2F4-E2F8 repress, E2F4 as part of the DREAM complex that also reads the adjacent CHR element. Sites sit in CpG-island promoters of replication and cell-cycle genes, and the RB-E2F axis is disabled in most human cancers.

MAF.name: MAF (MARE)
MAF.short: Maf proteins are basic region-leucine zipper factors that recognise an unusually long site, the Maf recognition element or MARE: 13 base pairs as TGCTGACTCAGCA, or 14 as TGCTGACGTCAGCA. The MARE is an AP-1 or CRE core with GC extensions added on both sides, and those extensions are read by two residues, an arginine and an asparagine, that are unique to the Maf basic region. The large Mafs - MAF, MAFA, MAFB and NRL - have transactivation domains; the small Mafs - MAFF, MAFG and MAFK - do not, so their homodimers repress and they serve instead as the obligate DNA-binding partners of the CNC and BACH proteins. Family members control lens, pancreatic beta cell, rod photoreceptor and erythroid programs, and are mutated or translocated in retinitis pigmentosa, insulinomatosis, carpotarsal osteolysis and myeloma.

HD_K50.name: K50 homeodomain (OTX/PITX/CRX-type, TAATCC)
HD_K50.short: A small group of homeodomains carries lysine instead of glutamine at position 50 of the domain, and that single substitution changes the two base pairs read 3' of the invariant TAAT core from TA to CC. The result is TAATCC, the bicoid-type site. In human the true K50 set is nine genes: OTX1, OTX2, CRX and DMBX1, PITX1, PITX2 and PITX3, and GSC and GSC2. They are tightly consistent - 34 motifs, all converging on TAATCC, with cooperative dimers on TAATCCGATTA - and unusually well supported in vitro. Paired-like factors that share their gene families but carry glutamine at position 50, such as RAX, VSX2, PHOX2B and NOBOX, read TAATTA and are covered by HD_Q50 instead.

CREB_ATF.name: CREB / ATF (CRE)
CREB_ATF.short: The CREB/ATF group contains the basic region-leucine zipper factors CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF7, ATF4 and CREB5. They bind the cyclic-AMP response element, the eight-base palindrome TGACGTCA, and its five-base half-site TGACG. The element was defined in the somatostatin promoter as the sequence through which cAMP raises transcription, and CREB1 phosphorylated on Ser133 recruits the coactivators CBP and p300 to it. Unlike the closely related AP-1 site, the CRE carries a central CpG, so its occupancy is sensitive to DNA methylation, and CRE-containing promoters are concentrated in CpG islands. Genome-wide, CREB occupies a few thousand promoters with a profile that is similar across tissues. All members read the same palindrome, so a match identifies the group rather than a single factor.

GATA.name: GATA
GATA.short: GATA factors are zinc-finger transcription factors that bind the six-base core WGATAA (usually AGATAA or TGATAA) through a single C4-type zinc finger plus a basic tail. Humans have six canonical members, GATA1-6, in two expression groups: GATA1/2/3 in blood, lymphocytes and mammary epithelium, GATA4/5/6 in heart, gut and gonad. The atypical protein TRPS1 carries one GATA-type finger and binds the same core as a repressor. Sites are short and very common, and are often read in pairs or next to an E-box occupied by TAL1. GATA binding sites underlie globin gene switching, cardiac septation and T-helper-2 commitment, and the factors are mutated in congenital heart disease, HDR syndrome and breast cancer.

RFX.name: RFX
RFX.short: RFX proteins recognize the X-box, a pseudo-palindrome built from two GTTRCC-like half-sites separated by zero to three bases. The DNA-binding domain is a 76-residue winged helix that reads bases with its beta-hairpin wing rather than with the usual recognition helix, and two domains bind one X-box cooperatively. Humans have eight members, RFX1-RFX8. RFX1-3 form homodimers and heterodimers and drive ciliary gene programs; RFX5 works in a complex with RFXAP and RFXANK to switch on MHC class II genes; RFX6 is restricted to pancreatic islet and enteroendocrine cells. The full 13-14 bp palindrome is one of the most information-rich motifs in vertebrate collections, which makes RFX hits unusually trustworthy.

MYC_MAX.name: MYC / MAX / MXD
MYC_MAX.short: MYC, MYCN and their obligate partner MAX bind the canonical E-box CACGTG as bHLH-LZ heterodimers, and the same site is bound by MAX homodimers and by the MAX-associated repressors MXD1-4, MXI1, MNT and MGA, which recruit Sin3-HDAC complexes. The related MLX branch (MondoA, ChREBP) reads an E-box with T/A flanks. The motif is a 6-bp palindrome, two CAC half-sites read by a histidine-glutamate-arginine triad in each basic region. MYC-MAX occupancy is concentrated in CpG-island promoters of already-active genes, which is why MYC is central to the growth program and why it is one of the most frequently activated oncogenes in human cancer. No member of the network can be told from another by sequence alone.

NFAT.name: NFAT
NFAT.short: NFAT sites are read by five proteins with a Rel-homology DNA-binding domain: the calcineurin-regulated NFATC1, NFATC2, NFATC3 and NFATC4, plus the structurally distinct, calcium-independent NFAT5 (TonEBP). Unlike NF-kB, the calcineurin-dependent NFATs bind as monomers to a short GGAAA core, usually written TGGAAA and only about six informative bases long. Because that is too little information to specify a site on its own, NFATs typically work in composite elements, most famously the NFAT-AP1 element of the interleukin-2 promoter, where NFAT and a Fos-Jun dimer touch each other on adjacent DNA. NFAT activity is controlled by dephosphorylation and nuclear import, which is why cyclosporin A and tacrolimus, which inhibit calcineurin, are immunosuppressive.

FOX_FHL.name: Divergent forkhead sites (FOXP dimeric / FHL)
FOX_FHL.short: This entry collects the forkhead factors whose preferred site is not the ordinary RYAAAYA element. Two things are going on. FOXN1 and FOXN4 read a completely unrelated five-base sequence, GACGC, called the forkhead-like or FHL motif, using the same recognition helix in a shifted register; FOXN2, FOXN3, FOXJ2 and FOXJ3 are bispecific and bind both FHL and canonical sites. Separately, the FOXP proteins (FOXP1-4) are the only forkheads that can form a domain-swapped dimer, and their highest-information models are a head-to-head pair of forkhead half-sites rather than a single one. The factors matter clinically: FOXN1 loss causes human athymic immunodeficiency, FOXP2 a speech disorder, and FOXP3 the autoimmune syndrome IPEX.

GLI.name: GLI
GLI.short: GLI factors are five-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger proteins that read the nine-base site GACCACCCA and form the transcriptional output of the Hedgehog pathway. Humans have three canonical members: GLI1, an activator that is itself a Hedgehog target gene, and GLI2 and GLI3, which are made as full-length activators but are partially degraded into N-terminal repressors when Hedgehog signaling is off. The related GLIS1, GLIS2 and GLIS3 proteins read a close variant, GACCCCCCAC. Binding is monomeric and the informative bases are concentrated at the 3' end of the site, which fingers four and five contact directly. GLI sites control limb and neural-tube patterning, and pathway mutations cause polydactyly syndromes, basal cell carcinoma and SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma.

PRDM.name: PRDM
PRDM.short: PRDM proteins are zinc-finger transcription factors defined by an N-terminal PR domain, a variant of the SET methyltransferase fold, followed by a tandem array of C2H2 zinc fingers that does the DNA binding. The family is heterogeneous and does not share one motif: each member's finger array reads its own sequence, and those sequences are unrelated to one another. The best-characterized members are PRDM1/BLIMP1, which binds an interferon-regulatory-factor-like AAAGTGAAAG site and drives plasma-cell differentiation; PRDM9, whose rapidly evolving finger array selects meiotic recombination hotspots and underlies a mouse hybrid-sterility phenotype; PRDM14, in naive pluripotency; and PRDM16, in brown adipocyte and craniofacial development. A hit labelled PRDM should be interpreted per member, never as a family-level call.

ATF6_CREB3.name: ATF6 / CREB3 (ER stress)
ATF6_CREB3.short: This group collects the endoplasmic-reticulum-tethered basic region-leucine zipper factors ATF6 and ATF6B together with the CREB3 (OASIS/Luman) family - CREB3, CREB3L1, CREB3L2, CREB3L3 and CREB3L4 - and XBP1. All are made as inactive precursors and released by regulated proteolysis or, for XBP1, by IRE1-mediated mRNA splicing, so their activity reports stress in the secretory pathway rather than a signaling kinase. They bind an asymmetric, CRE-like element, TGACGTGG, equivalently CCACGTCA on the opposite strand, whose CCACG half is the ATF6-contacted part of the ER stress response element ERSE (CCAAT-N9-CCACG). Their targets are ER chaperones, ERAD components and secretory-pathway genes. The members are not separable by sequence, and several of their matrices are indistinguishable from an ordinary CRE or a CACGTG E-box.

HAND_TWIST.name: TWIST / HAND
HAND_TWIST.short: TWIST1/2, HAND1/2, TCF21, SCX and MESP1/2 are class II basic helix-loop-helix factors of mesoderm and neural crest. They bind the E-box CANNTG as heterodimers with the ubiquitous E-proteins TCF3/TCF4/TCF12, with each other, or as homodimers, and this group prefers CAGATG (CATCTG on the opposite strand). Because the two central E-box bases are barely contacted by the protein, the distinction from the muscle E-box CAGCTG and the neural CATATG is weak. TWIST has one genuinely diagnostic feature: a double E-box with the two boxes five bases apart, which aligns two TWIST-E47 dimers on one face of the helix so they can tetramerise. The family runs craniofacial, cardiac, tendon and epithelial-mesenchymal transition programmes.

HES_HEY.name: HES / HEY (N-box)
HES_HEY.short: HES1-7, HEY1/2, HEYL and HELT are the vertebrate hairy/Enhancer-of-split relatives: bHLH repressors with an Orange domain that sets partner choice and a C-terminal WRPW or YRPW peptide that recruits TLE/Groucho corepressors. Most are direct Notch targets, so their activity reports Notch signalling. They read a genuinely different site from the class II bHLH activators — a proline in the basic region shifts preference away from CANNTG. Two sites are described: the functionally defined N box CACNAG, and the higher-affinity CACGYG (CACGTG or CACGCG) that the database matrices actually capture. HES1 autorepression through N boxes generates a two-hour expression oscillation; HES7 drives the somite segmentation clock.

STAT.name: STAT
STAT.short: The seven human STAT proteins - STAT1, STAT2, STAT3, STAT4, STAT5A, STAT5B and STAT6 - sit latent in the cytoplasm until a receptor-associated JAK kinase phosphorylates a single C-terminal tyrosine. Two phosphorylated monomers then pair through reciprocal SH2-phosphotyrosine contacts and clamp around DNA at a gamma-interferon activation site (GAS): the short inverted repeat TTCNNNGAA. Spacing is almost the only sequence feature that distinguishes them, with STAT6 preferring a four-base spacer and the rest a three-base spacer, so a GAS match names the family and not the member. STATs convert essentially every cytokine, interferon and several growth factor signals into transcription, and germline or somatic STAT mutations cause immunodeficiency, allergy, growth failure and leukemia.

CEBP.name: C/EBP
CEBP.short: The C/EBP family - CEBPA, CEBPB (NF-IL6), CEBPD, CEBPE, CEBPG, with DDIT3 (CHOP) as a heterodimer partner - binds the palindromic element TT(G/A)CGCAA, most often written as the 10-mer ATTGCGCAAT. These are basic region-leucine zipper proteins; the leucine zipper itself was first described in C/EBP, and the family's distinctive DNA contacts centre on an arginine that is conserved in C/EBPs but not in other bZIPs. Family members control hepatic and adipose metabolism, the acute-phase response, and granulocyte maturation, and CEBPA and CEBPE are mutated in human myeloid disease. The paralogues are indistinguishable from sequence. The boundary with the CREB/ATF family is genuinely blurred: CHOP-containing dimers and ATF4 read a hybrid half-C/EBP, half-CRE site, and CpG methylation converts a CRE into a C/EBP-alpha site.

ETS_EHF.name: ETS epithelial (ELF/EHF)
ETS_EHF.short: ELF1, ELF2, ELF3, ELF4, ELF5 and EHF are the ELF branch of the ETS family. They bind the same GGA(A/T) core as every other ETS protein through the same winged helix-turn-helix domain, but prefer a C where class I ETS factors prefer an A three bases 5' of the core, giving the ten-base site ACCCGGAAGT. ELF3, ELF5 and EHF are the epithelium-specific "ESE" members, expressed in gut, salivary gland, breast, airway, cornea, prostate and bladder epithelium; ELF1, ELF2 and ELF4 are broader, with strong hematopoietic expression. These factors set and maintain epithelial differentiation - mammary alveolar cell fate, intestinal goblet cells, airway CFTR expression - and are recurrently mutated or silenced in carcinomas of the bladder, biliary tract, cervix and breast.

HSF.name: HSF
HSF.short: Heat shock factors bind the heat shock element (HSE), an array of the 5-base unit nGAAn in alternating orientation: nTTCn-nGAAn-nTTCn and longer runs. The DNA-binding domain is a winged helix, and HSF proteins trimerize through a coiled coil so that three subunits each read one 5-base unit, with further trimers loading cooperatively onto longer arrays. Humans have HSF1, HSF2, HSF4, HSF5 and the Y-linked HSFY1/HSFY2. HSF1 is the stress-inducible member, held inactive as a monomer until proteotoxic stress triggers trimerization. HSEs drive heat shock protein genes, and HSF1 activity also supports malignant transformation; HSF4 mutations cause congenital cataract.

ZIC.name: ZIC
ZIC.short: ZIC1 to ZIC5 are five-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger proteins whose DNA-binding domains are the closest relatives of GLI outside the GLIS subfamily, and which read a GLI-like site. In vitro selection gives an optimal ZIC site almost identical to the GLI consensus but bound with lower affinity; modern high-throughput measurements extend it to GACCCCCCGCTGTG, whose reverse complement, CACAGCAGGGGGT, is how several databases write the same motif. ZIC proteins also bind GLI zinc fingers directly and can raise or lower GLI-dependent transcription. They act mainly in dorsal neural tube, neural crest, somites and cerebellum, and human mutations cause holoprosencephaly (ZIC2), X-linked heterotaxy (ZIC3) and Dandy-Walker malformation (ZIC1 with ZIC4).

ZNF24.name: ZNF24 / ZSCAN-type promoter ZFs
ZNF24.short: A small group of SCAN-domain C2H2 zinc fingers with defined, experimentally supported binding sites at promoters and microsatellites: ZNF24 (also known as ZNF191 and ZSCAN3), ZSCAN4, ZSCAN21, ZSCAN22, ZSCAN29, ZKSCAN1 and ZKSCAN3. They are grouped by domain architecture and a promoter-proximal style of binding, not by a shared motif: the seven proteins read at least five unrelated sequences. ZNF24 binds a TCAT tetranucleotide repeat, ZSCAN4 a CA-repeat core, ZSCAN29 an inverted pair of GTCTAC hexamers, ZKSCAN3 GGCTAGCCC and ZKSCAN1 CCTACTATG. Reported functions are equally varied, from repressing VEGFA transcription to repressing autophagy genes and protecting telomeres in early embryos.

GRHL.name: Grainyhead (GRHL)
GRHL.short: The Grainyhead/CP2 family binds the palindrome AACCGGTT through an immunoglobulin-like DNA-binding domain that shares a fold with p53 but differs from it in important details. Six human members split into two branches: the epithelial GRHL1, GRHL2 and GRHL3, and the more broadly expressed TFCP2 (LSF/CP2), TFCP2L1 and UBP1 (LBP-1a). They bind as dimers, and many real elements are doubled, giving 16-26 bp tandem sites. GRHL factors control epidermal barrier formation, neural tube and palate closure, and epithelial identity, and they sit at the epithelial end of EMT regulation. Human mutations cause Van der Woude syndrome and nonsyndromic cleft palate.

AP2.name: AP-2 (TFAP2)
AP2.short: The five human TFAP2 proteins (TFAP2A-E, historically AP-2 alpha through epsilon) bind a pseudo-palindrome made of GCC and GGC triplets separated by exactly three bases. Each subunit contributes a basic region that inserts a loop into the major groove, and the two subunits are held together by a helix-span-helix domain; the factors are constitutive dimers even off DNA, and all paralogue combinations heterodimerize. The site is GC-rich and sits in GC-rich promoters and neural crest enhancers. TFAP2 factors behave as pioneer factors during neural crest specification, and mutations cause branchio-oculo-facial syndrome (TFAP2A) and Char syndrome (TFAP2B). A hit identifies the family, not a paralogue.

MYB.name: MYB / MYB-like
MYB.short: MYB factors bind the Myb binding site (MBS), a six-base element written YAACKG, through two or three imperfect ~52-residue repeats that each fold into a helix-turn-helix-like unit. Humans have three true MYB proteins: MYB (c-Myb), MYBL1 (A-Myb) and MYBL2 (B-Myb). Only repeats R2 and R3 are required for sequence-specific binding, and their recognition helices sit side by side in one major groove. MYB proteins control hematopoietic progenitor expansion, spermatogenesis and, for MYBL2, mitotic gene expression through the MuvB complex. MYB is duplicated in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and fused to NFIB in adenoid cystic carcinoma. This family key also collects Myb/SANT-fold archetypes whose proteins are not MYB factors and do not bind the MBS, which is the main source of confusion here.

NFE2_BACH.name: NFE2 / NRF / BACH (ARE)
NFE2_BACH.short: This family covers the cap-n-collar (CNC) basic region-leucine zipper activators NFE2, NFE2L1 (NRF1) and NFE2L2 (NRF2) together with the BTB-bZIP repressors BACH1 and BACH2. None of them binds DNA alone: each must heterodimerize with a small Maf protein (MAFF, MAFG or MAFK). The resulting element is the antioxidant or electrophile response element, TGACTCAGCA, an AP-1-like TGAC half-site read by the CNC or BACH subunit joined to a GC-extended half read by the small Maf. It is therefore a one-sided version of the Maf recognition element. NRF2 drives the cytoprotective gene battery and is constitutively activated by KEAP1 loss in several cancers; NFE2 is required for platelet formation; BACH1 is a heme sensor and BACH2 a lymphocyte regulator. Members cannot be distinguished from sequence.

NR_STEROID.name: Steroid receptors (GR/MR/PR/AR)
NR_STEROID.short: The steroid receptors - glucocorticoid receptor (GR/NR3C1), mineralocorticoid receptor (MR/NR3C2), progesterone receptor (PGR) and androgen receptor (AR) - are hormone-activated transcription factors that bind DNA as homodimers on a 15 bp inverted repeat: two copies of the hexamer AGAACA facing each other across a 3 bp spacer, written AGAACAnnnTGTTCT. All four receptors read essentially the same element, so a match identifies the steroid-receptor group and not a particular receptor. Which receptor occupies a site in a given cell is decided by hormone availability, receptor expression, pioneer factors such as FOXA1 and pre-existing chromatin accessibility, not by sequence. These elements carry the transcriptional response to cortisol, aldosterone, progesterone and androgens, and they are the DNA end of drugs from dexamethasone to the antiandrogens used in prostate cancer.

NR2F_COUP.name: COUP-TF (NR2F)
aka: chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor
NR2F_COUP.short: COUP-TFI (NR2F1), COUP-TFII (NR2F2) and EAR2 (NR2F6) are orphan nuclear receptors that bind DNA as homodimers, most often on a DR1: two AGGTCA half-sites in the same orientation separated by one base pair. Their distinguishing property is not a private consensus but promiscuity - the same dimer accommodates direct repeats with several spacings, plus inverted and everted arrangements of the same hexamer - which is how COUP-TFs compete with vitamin D, thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptors for shared elements and repress them. The three paralogues share one motif and are also not separable from RXR homodimers, HNF4/TR2-TR4 or ERR sites. COUP-TFII specifies venous identity and is required for angiogenesis; NR2F1 mutations cause an optic atrophy and intellectual disability syndrome.

NFI.name: NFI (CTF/NF-1)
NFI.short: Nuclear factor I proteins bind a 15-bp palindrome, TTGGC followed by five variable bases and GCCAA. Four human genes, NFIA, NFIB, NFIC and NFIX, encode DNA-binding domains that are about 85% identical, so they bind as homodimers or heterodimers in any combination and cannot be told apart from sequence. The domain adopts a SMAD MH1-like fold with a bound zinc ion, which is why the family is classified with SMAD rather than with any CCAAT-box factor. The full palindrome is highly informative, but NFI also occupies single TTGGC half-sites. NFI factors keep stem cell populations in glia, retina, skin and muscle on track, and are mutated in human overgrowth and brain malformation syndromes.

MBD_CXXC.name: MBD and CxxC readers
MBD_CXXC.short: This family puts two opposite kinds of reader in one place. MBD proteins - MECP2, MBD1, MBD3 - bind CpG that is methylated. ZF-CxxC proteins - CXXC1/CFP1, CXXC4, CXXC5, KDM2A, KDM2B, FBXL19, TET1, TET3, DNMT1, KMT2A, KMT2B - bind CpG that is not. Neither group has a sequence-specific site in any useful sense. The single most important thing to know about this page is that its motifs are essentially measurements of CpG density: the family consensus is literally CG, eight of the twenty-one models carry two to four bits of information, and the representative model is a two-base-pair CG. Treat a MECP2 motif in particular with real scepticism.

HD_SIX.name: SIX
HD_SIX.short: The six human SIX genes encode homeodomain proteins with an additional SIX domain that recruits the EYA family of transcriptional coactivators. Their shared DNA core is TGATAC (GTATCA on the other strand), usually embedded in a longer element written GTAACCTGATAC, which on the opposite strand contains the MEF3 site TCAGGTT first defined in the myogenin promoter. SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 partner with EYA proteins and activate transcription; SIX3 and SIX6 instead recruit Groucho/TLE corepressors and repress. The family builds muscle, kidney, inner ear and eye: SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal syndrome, SIX3 mutations cause holoprosencephaly, and SIX1 with EYA is re-activated in several carcinomas.

SMAD.name: SMAD
SMAD.short: SMAD proteins are the intracellular effectors of TGF-beta family signaling. Their MH1 domain inserts a beta-hairpin into the major groove and reads just four bases, GTCT or its reverse complement AGAC, often written as the CAGAC box or as the 8-bp palindrome GTCTAGAC. SMAD3, SMAD4 and the BMP-activated SMAD1/5/9 also bind a separate 5-bp GC-rich element, GGCGC or GGCCG. Both elements are far too short to be informative alone, and genome-wide SMAD occupancy is set mainly by whichever lineage-determining factor is present, so most SMAD ChIP peaks are better explained by a partner's motif than by an SBE. This is a family where a motif hit needs corroboration more than almost any other.

DMRT.name: DMRT (DM domain)
DMRT.short: DMRT proteins are the DM-domain transcription factors, named after Drosophila Doublesex and C. elegans MAB-3, the sexual regulators in which the domain was found. Humans have seven well-studied genes, DMRT1, DMRT2, DMRT3, DMRTA1, DMRTA2, DMRTB1 and DMRTC2, plus DMRTC1 paralogues. The DM domain is not a classical zinc finger: two zinc ions are chelated by an intertwined arrangement of cysteines and histidines that cannot be split into independent fingers, and the module ends in a recognition helix. The proteins bind a pseudopalindromic element built from two ACA/TGT half-sites, canonically ACAWTGTW, as dimers and higher-order oligomers. DMRT1 is required for testis differentiation and sustains it after birth; it is the sex-determining gene in chicken, and the 9p24 region containing it is deleted in human 46,XY sex reversal.

CHROMATIN.name: Chromatin regulators without a classical DBD
aka: Chromatin regulators without a classical DBD
ChIP-derived motifs of readers and writers
CHROMATIN.short: A deliberate holding bucket, and the place to learn why a ChIP-derived motif may not belong to the protein it is labelled with. The twenty motifs here are attributed to chromatin readers, writers and scaffolds that have no sequence-specific DNA-binding domain: BPTF, PHF1, PHF21A, DPF1, MYSM1, SETBP1, TOPORS, GATAD2A, ZFPM1, ZZZ3, GLYR1, MTF2, TCF20, SP140L, NAIF1 and ARID1A. Cohesion is 0.38, the lowest in the atlas, and six models are explicitly flagged as resembling another family. The clearest case is ZFPM1/FOG-1, which binds GATA-1's zinc finger rather than DNA, yet carries a GATA motif. Read this page as a warning list.

HIF_ARNT.name: HIF / ARNT
HIF_ARNT.short: The hypoxia response element is the site read by HIF, a heterodimer of an oxygen-labile alpha subunit (HIF-1alpha, HIF-2alpha/EPAS1, HIF-3alpha) and the constitutive beta subunit ARNT (HIF-1beta) or its paralogue ARNT2. Both partners are bHLH-PAS proteins. The element is an asymmetric E-box half-site pair: ARNT reads the 3' GTG and the alpha subunit reads a 5' half that is usually TAC or GAC, giving the five-base core (A/G)CGTG, most often written in context as ...TACGTGC... When oxygen is plentiful the alpha subunits are prolyl-hydroxylated and destroyed by the VHL ubiquitin ligase, so occupancy of these sites is a direct readout of oxygen availability. HIF drives erythropoietin, VEGFA and the glycolytic genes, and the pathway is constitutively active in VHL-mutant kidney cancer.

HNF4.name: HNF4
HNF4.short: HNF4A and HNF4G are nuclear receptors that bind DNA only as homodimers, on a DR1: two hexameric half-sites in the same orientation separated by exactly one base pair. Their preferred half-site drifts away from the superfamily's AGGTCA towards AG(G/T)CCA, which is why the databases render the HNF4 motif as CAAAGTCCA, or at full length as a 13 bp DR1. That drift is real specificity: the HNF4-specific binding motif is bound by HNF4A and not by other nuclear receptors tested in vivo. The same family here also holds NR2C1 and NR2C2 (TR2/TR4), whose models are generic AGGTCA DR1s and are not distinguishable from RXR or COUP-TF. HNF4A is the central regulator of hepatocyte, islet and intestinal gene expression and the MODY1 gene.

MEF2.name: MEF2
MEF2.short: MEF2 sites are bound by the four MADS-box factors MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D, which act as obligate dimers. The element is an A/T-rich decamer, CTA(A/T)4TAG, and is easy to confuse with ordinary AT-rich sequence: the information sits almost entirely in the flanking CTA and TAG. MEF2 and SRF share the MADS fold but not the site - SRF requires the CC and GG of a CArG box where MEF2 requires TA and TA. The four paralogues have the same sequence preference and overlapping expression, so which one acts at a given element is decided by cell type and by chromatin rather than by DNA. MEF2 factors drive muscle differentiation, cardiac morphogenesis and activity-dependent programmes in neurons.

HD_CUT.name: CUX (CUT homeodomain)
HD_CUT.short: CUX1, CUX2 and the SATB proteins SATB1 and SATB2 bind DNA with two kinds of domain at once: CUT repeats, each an independent ~70-residue DNA-binding module, plus a homeodomain. The combination shifts the preferred site away from the generic TAAT core of other homeodomain proteins toward ATCGAT, usually embedded in a longer near-palindrome such as TAATCGATTA. CUT repeats also bind CCAAT boxes, which is how CUX1 earned its older name, CCAAT displacement protein. SATB1 and SATB2 use their CUT-like domain differently, recognizing AT-rich matrix-attachment regions rather than ATCGAT. CUX1 is a haploinsufficient tumor suppressor in myeloid and other cancers, and SATB1 and SATB2 organize chromatin over long distances in T cells and bone.

HD_ONECUT.name: ONECUT (HNF6)
HD_ONECUT.short: ONECUT1 (HNF6), ONECUT2 and ONECUT3 bind DNA with a single CUT domain joined to a divergent homeodomain, and the two modules together read TATTGATT, often followed by a run of T. The same proteins also bind ATCGAT, the core preferred by the CUX proteins, and both forms appear across JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP. This is the most internally consistent family in the CUT class: cohesion is 0.92 and the three paralogues cannot be told apart from sequence. ONECUT1 is a liver, pancreas and biliary factor whose loss disrupts bile duct and endocrine pancreas development and causes human diabetes; ONECUT2 has become a target of interest in treatment-resistant and neuroendocrine prostate cancer.

TCF_LEF.name: TCF/LEF (HMG box)
TCF_LEF.short: TCF/LEF proteins are the DNA-binding end of the canonical Wnt pathway. Humans have four: TCF7 (TCF-1), TCF7L1 (TCF-3), TCF7L2 (TCF-4) and LEF1. Each binds DNA through a single SRY-type HMG box plus an adjacent basic region, reading the minor groove of the Wnt response element CTTTGWW and bending the helix sharply. None activates transcription on its own: an N-terminal domain recruits beta-catenin, which supplies the coactivators, and without nuclear beta-catenin the same proteins repress through TLE/Groucho. Wnt response elements control intestinal crypt renewal, hair follicle and limb development, and T cell differentiation; they are constitutively occupied in APC-mutant colorectal cancer, and an intronic variant at TCF7L2 is the largest-effect common risk allele for type 2 diabetes.

SNAI.name: SNAIL / SCRATCH
SNAI.short: The SNAIL/SCRATCH proteins - SNAI1 (Snail), SNAI2 (Slug), SNAI3 (Smuc), SCRT1 and SCRT2 - are C2H2 zinc-finger repressors that read the E-box CAGGTG, the same 6 bp core that basic helix-loop-helix activators use. They carry no HLH domain; specificity comes from four or five zinc fingers, and repression from an N-terminal SNAG peptide that recruits LSD1/CoREST. SNAI1 and SNAI2 repress E-cadherin and drive epithelial-mesenchymal transition in gastrulation, neural crest migration, fibrosis and carcinoma; SCRT1 and SCRT2 do related work in neurons. SCRATCH sites carry an extra CAAC, giving the only sequence feature that separates part of this family. SNAI2 deletion causes Waardenburg syndrome type 2D and piebaldism.

MYOD.name: Myogenic bHLH (MyoD)
MYOD.short: The four myogenic regulatory factors — MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6 (MRF4) and MYOG — plus the related repressor MSC (musculin/MyoR) are class II basic helix-loop-helix proteins restricted to the skeletal muscle lineage. They bind DNA as heterodimers with the ubiquitous class I E-proteins TCF3, TCF4 and TCF12, reading the E-box CAGCTG with a preference for A/T-rich flanks (AACAGCTGTT). MYOD1 was the first transcription factor shown to reprogram cell identity: transfecting it alone converts fibroblasts into myoblasts. Whether a myogenic bHLH activates muscle genes depends less on where it binds than on three residues in its basic region — the "myogenic code" — so an occupied E-box and an active one are not the same thing.

TEAD.name: TEAD
TEAD.short: The four human TEAD proteins (TEAD1-4, formerly TEF-1, TEF-4, TEF-5 and TEF-3) bind the MCAT element GGAATG, read on the other strand as CATTCC. The DNA-binding TEA domain is a three-helix bundle with a homeodomain-like fold, and two TEADs load cooperatively onto tandem MCAT sites. TEADs have no activation domain of their own: they are the DNA-binding platform for the Hippo pathway coactivators YAP and TAZ, and for the VGLL proteins that compete with them. The motif is therefore the readout of Hippo signaling status on chromatin. TEAD sites drive muscle gene expression, trophectoderm specification and organ size control, and are central to YAP-driven cancers.

HD_IRX.name: IRX (TALE, Iroquois)
HD_IRX.short: IRX1 through IRX6, with the related factor MKX (Mohawk), form the Iroquois branch of the TALE homeodomain superclass - homeodomains carrying three extra residues between helices 1 and 2. Unlike most homeodomain proteins they do not read a TAAT core. Their recognition unit is a short ACA, and the functional site is an inverted repeat of it, so models in these databases range from the half-site CATGT up to long palindromes such as ACATGnnnnnCATGT. The IRX genes sit in two clusters, IRX1/2/4 and IRX3/5/6, and pattern the heart, limb, kidney and nervous system. IRX3 is best known outside developmental biology as the gene connected by long-range enhancer contacts to the obesity-associated variants inside FTO.

HD_CDX_PDX.name: CDX / PDX / anterior gut HD
HD_CDX_PDX.short: This family groups the caudal-related factors CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 with PDX1, all encoded by ParaHox genes - an ancient cluster that is the evolutionary sister of the Hox cluster. The CDX proteins read TTTATG, usually extended to TTTATGGC, a site distinct enough to be recognizable. PDX1 is a different case: its in vitro motif is plain TAATTA, indistinguishable from the generic Q50 homeodomain site, so PDX1 specificity in vivo comes from partners rather than from the sequence it prefers. CDX2 patterns the posterior gut and is the standard immunohistochemical marker of intestinal epithelium; PDX1 is required for pancreas development and its loss causes pancreatic agenesis and MODY4.

ETV2_ETV6.name: ETV2 / ETV6-type
ETV2_ETV6.short: ETV2 (ER71), ETV6 (TEL) and ETV7 (TEL2) are ETS-domain proteins that read the same GGA(A/T) core as the rest of the family. ETV2 is a transient activator required for the specification of blood and endothelium; ETV6 and ETV7 are repressors, and ETV6 spreads repression by polymerizing through its PNT/SAM domain. They are grouped here because their motif models cluster together, not because they share a distinct binding preference: ETV2's selected sequence is the ordinary class I ETS site and ETV6/ETV7 differ from it only marginally. What does recur among these models is arrangement - several are two GGAA cores in tandem or head-to-head. ETV6 is one of the most frequently rearranged genes in leukemia, most famously as ETV6-RUNX1 in childhood B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

NFKB.name: NF-kB / Rel
NFKB.short: The kB site is the element read by the five mammalian Rel/NF-kB proteins: NFKB1 (p105/p50), NFKB2 (p100/p52), RELA (p65), RELB and REL (c-Rel). They bind DNA only as dimers, through a shared Rel-homology region, so the site is pseudo-palindromic and is usually written GGGRNNYYCC, each subunit reading one guanine-rich half. What makes these factors unusual is that they are pre-made and held in the cytoplasm by IkB proteins, then released within minutes by inflammatory cytokines, microbial sensing, antigen receptors or DNA damage. The same kB site can therefore be empty in a resting cell and heavily occupied after stimulation. kB sites lie in promoters and enhancers of cytokine, chemokine, adhesion-molecule and pro-survival genes, and are the usual first evidence that a regulatory region is inflammation-responsive.

RUNX.name: RUNX
RUNX.short: RUNX sites are read by RUNX1, RUNX2 and RUNX3 through the Runt domain, a 128-residue immunoglobulin-like fold in the same structural class as NF-kB and p53. The core is a six-base element, TGYGGT, written ACCRCA on the other strand, and it is the retroviral enhancer "core" site originally described for core-binding factor. None of the three proteins binds efficiently alone: all require the non-DNA-binding subunit CBFB, which clamps the Runt domain into its DNA-bound conformation and raises affinity substantially. RUNX1 is the hematopoietic member and one of the most frequent targets of chromosomal translocation in leukemia; RUNX2 controls osteoblast differentiation and RUNX3 gut and immune programmes. The three paralogues are indistinguishable by sequence preference.

CENPB_POGO.name: CENP-B / pogo / Tigger
CENPB_POGO.short: The third and largest of the atlas's domesticated-transposase families. CENP-B, the Tigger-derived TIGD1 to TIGD7 proteins, POGK, JRK and CENPBD1 all carry DNA-binding domains descended from pogo, a Drosophila DNA transposon whose Tigger relatives left more than a hundred thousand fossil copies in the human genome. CENP-B itself recognizes the 17-base-pair CENP-B box, which recurs in alpha-satellite DNA - so a CENP-B box match is almost always centromeric or pericentromeric, not a regulatory site. Sixteen motifs cover twelve symbols, most of them sharing a bipartite pattern of a TTCG/CGAA block and a CCCG/CGGG block read by two helix-turn-helix domains. Cohesion is low at 0.48 and one model is flagged suspect.

HD_PRD_LIKE.name: PRD-like / primate-specific (CRX-like)
HD_PRD_LIKE.short: PRD-like homeobox genes are a small set of rapidly evolving, single-homeodomain factors, ARGFX, DPRX, LEUTX, TPRX1 and RHOXF1/2 among them, that are expressed almost exclusively in the oocyte, the cleavage-stage embryo and the germ line. Several arose by retrotransposition of a CRX-like ancestor within mammals, and several have been lost or pseudogenised in other lineages, so there are no mouse orthologues for much of the group. Most of them select a short K50-type homeodomain site, TAATCC, in vitro; ARGFX instead prefers a TAATTA palindrome. They are candidate drivers of human zygotic genome activation, acting at promoters derived from endogenous retroviral repeats. The evidence base is thin and largely in vitro, and the motifs are short.

PAR_BZIP.name: PAR bZIP (HLF/NFIL3/DBP)
PAR_BZIP.short: The PAR bZIP group contains three proline- and acidic-amino-acid-rich basic region-leucine zipper activators - DBP (albumin D-site binding protein), HLF (hepatic leukemia factor) and TEF - together with NFIL3 (E4BP4), which lacks the PAR domain, represses rather than activates, and yet reads the same site. That site is the palindrome TTACGTAA, written in much of the literature as TTATG(T/C)AA. It differs from the cyclic-AMP response element at only the outermost bases of each half-site, TTAC in place of TGAC. DBP, HLF and TEF accumulate with circadian rhythms in liver and suprachiasmatic nucleus, and NFIL3 oscillates in antiphase, so the same element can be activated or repressed depending on time of day. This is the most internally consistent bZIP family in the collection, and its four members are indistinguishable by sequence.

SAND.name: SAND domain (AIRE/SP100/GMEB)
SAND.short: The SAND domain is a small DNA-binding fold named after the four proteins in which it was first recognized: Sp100, AIRE, NucP41/75 and DEAF1. Sequence-specific binding depends on a conserved KDWK motif on the domain's surface, and only some SAND proteins have it. The best-defined members are GMEB1 and GMEB2, which bind as a heterodimer, also known as parvovirus initiation factor, to two CpG-containing tetranucleotide half-sites with flexible spacing: ACGY-N(1-9)-RCGY, with an optimum spacer of six bases. Binding is abolished by methylation of the CpG in either half-site. AIRE and the speckled proteins SP100 and SP140 lack the KDWK motif and are recruited through chromatin rather than sequence, so motif models attributed to them should be treated as descriptions of where they were found.

EGR.name: EGR
EGR.short: EGR1 to EGR4 are immediate-early transcription factors whose three C2H2 zinc fingers read a nine-base GC-rich site, GCGTGGGCG, also written GCGGGGGCG. The first of these proteins, EGR1, is better known to structural biologists as Zif268: its complex with DNA was the crystal structure that established how zinc fingers recognize DNA, three bases per finger, and it remains the reference for the C2H2 recognition code. EGR proteins are induced within minutes by growth factors, serum and neuronal activity, so their sites sit in the promoters of rapidly inducible genes. All four paralogues share the same matrix, and the WT1 tumor suppressor binds essentially the same sequence, so a hit names a site rather than a protein.

MITF_TFE.name: MITF / TFE (CLEAR)
MITF_TFE.short: MITF, TFE3, TFEB and TFEC are bHLH-LZ factors that dimerize only with each other, because a three-residue insertion kinks their leucine zipper. They read a canonical E-box core with a strict flanking requirement, giving the palindromic 10-mer GTCACGTGAC - the same element known as the melanocyte M-box (TCATGTGA) in pigmentation genes and as the CLEAR box in lysosomal and autophagy promoters. MITF is the lineage factor of melanocytes and is mutated in Waardenburg syndrome type 2A and predisposes to melanoma; TFEB and TFE3 run the lysosome-autophagy program downstream of mTORC1 and are recurrently rearranged in renal cell carcinoma. The four paralogues cannot be told apart from sequence.

YY1.name: YY1 / YY2
YY1.short: YY1 is a ubiquitously expressed zinc-finger protein that binds a short CCAT-centered site, usually written CGCCATNTT or, on the other strand, AANATGGCGGC. It sits at or just inside the transcription start site of a large fraction of CpG-island promoters, works as an activator at some and a repressor at others, and is found on both the enhancer and the promoter side of enhancer-promoter contacts. Two retrogenes derived from YY1, YY2 and ZFP42/REX1, share the same zinc-finger domain; YY2 binds the same consensus more weakly, and REX1 prefers divergent sites that still contain the CCAT core. Because the motif is short and concentrated in CpG islands, a YY1 match is one of the most common hits in promoter sequence.

E_PROTEIN.name: E-proteins (TCF3/4/12)
E_PROTEIN.short: TCF3 (E2A/E12/E47), TCF4 (E2-2) and TCF12 (HEB) are the broadly expressed class I bHLH proteins that serve as the general dimerization partners for tissue-restricted bHLH factors - MYOD in muscle, ASCL and NEUROD in neurons, TWIST in mesenchyme, TAL1 in blood - and are sequestered by ID proteins. They bind the class-A E-box, written CACCTG or equivalently CAGGTG, and also CAGCTG. Because most functional sites are heterodimeric, only one half-site is read by the E-protein itself. E2A loss abolishes B-cell development; TCF4 haploinsufficiency causes Pitt-Hopkins syndrome, TCF12 loss causes coronal craniosynostosis, and TCF3 is a recurrent fusion partner in pre-B leukaemia.

P53.name: p53 family
P53.short: The p53 response element is bound by three paralogues - TP53, TP63 and TP73 - through a shared, structurally unusual DNA-binding domain that works only as a tetramer. The element is built from two decamers of the form RRRCWWGYYY, usually adjacent but tolerating a spacer, so a full site is 20 bp or more. Each decamer is read by a p53 dimer, and the CATG core at its centre is the part that matters: three of the four hotspot residues mutated in human cancers contact exactly this DNA. Because the element is long and its core is well defined, p53 sites are among the more specific vertebrate motifs, and a good double-decamer match is genuinely informative. What a match cannot tell you is which of the three paralogues is responsible.

HD_ATYPICAL.name: Atypical / composite homeodomain
HD_ATYPICAL.short: This family collects homeodomains that do not behave like homeodomains. Instead of one small domain in a compact protein, these factors bury one to five divergent homeodomains inside large multidomain proteins, usually alongside many C2H2 zinc fingers: ZHX1-3, ZFHX2 and ZFHX3, HOMEZ, TSHZ1-3, HMBOX1, HDX, HHEX, and the SATB-type CUT-plus-homeodomain proteins. Several were discovered as something else entirely, an AT-rich enhancer-binding protein, a telomere repeat-binding protein, a chromatin scaffold protein. Their motifs are correspondingly heterogeneous: there is no single family consensus, several database models carry almost no information, and where a good motif exists it may be read by the zinc fingers rather than by the homeodomain. Useful as a bucket, not as an identifier.

SREBF.name: SREBP
SREBF.short: SREBP-1 and SREBP-2 are bHLH-LZ factors made as ER membrane precursors and activated by sterol-regulated proteolysis, so only the cleaved nuclear fragment binds DNA. They are unusual in having dual specificity: a tyrosine replaces the arginine that is otherwise invariant in bHLH basic regions, letting them bind both the palindromic E-box CACGTG and the non-palindromic sterol regulatory element SRE-1, TCACNCCAC. Sites sit in promoters of cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis genes and work with a neighbouring NF-Y CCAAT box or SP1 GC box, which an isolated SRE needs for activity. The pathway controls the LDL receptor, hepatic lipogenesis and the response to statins, and is central to fatty liver disease and insulin resistance.

CLOCK_BMAL.name: CLOCK / BMAL1
CLOCK_BMAL.short: CLOCK, BMAL1 (gene symbol ARNTL) and NPAS2 are basic helix-loop-helix PER-ARNT-SIM (bHLH-PAS) transcription factors that form the activating limb of the mammalian circadian clock. BMAL1 pairs with CLOCK or with its paralogue NPAS2 and binds the palindromic E-box CACGTG together with a small set of E-box-like variants. The complex reads seven base pairs rather than six, because a flanking A-T pair next to the core contributes to affinity. Strong circadian promoters usually carry two E-boxes in tandem six to seven base pairs apart, and it is the pair, not a single hexamer, that produces rhythmic transcription. Occupancy oscillates once a day and drives Per, Cry, Rev-erb and thousands of output genes. Because CACGTG is also the core read by MYC/MAX, USF and SREBP, sequence alone cannot assign an E-box to the clock.

SPI1.name: SPI1 / SPIB / SPIC (PU.1)
SPI1.short: SPI1 (PU.1), SPIB and SPIC are the class III branch of the ETS family. They read the same GGA(A/T) core as other ETS proteins but demand a purine-rich 5' flank, giving the hematopoietic PU-box AAAGAGGAAGTG - the one ETS subfamily that a scan can usually tell apart from the rest. SPI1 is required for macrophage, neutrophil, dendritic cell and B-cell development; SPIB acts in B cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells; SPIC specifies red pulp macrophages. PU.1 also nucleates the ETS-IRF composite element (EICE), GGAAGTGAAAC, by recruiting IRF4 or IRF8 to DNA it has already bound. Reduced PU.1 dosage causes acute myeloid leukemia in mice, and SPI1 fusions occur in high-risk pediatric T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

ZBTB7.name: ZBTB7A/B/C (LRF)
ZBTB7.short: ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C are BTB/POZ zinc-finger proteins that read short GC-rich sites through four C2H2 fingers and repress or reorganize promoters through the dimerizing BTB domain. ZBTB7A, also called LRF, Pokemon or FBI-1, competes with SP1 at GC boxes, represses the ARF tumor suppressor and the fetal hemoglobin genes, and acts more broadly as a promoter-accessibility factor for other transcription factors. ZBTB7B, better known as ThPOK or cKrox, directs CD4 rather than CD8 T-cell fate and has been proposed as the vertebrate GAGA factor. Because the recognition sites are short, GC-rich and shared with the large SP/KLF motif class, hits in this family are easy to obtain and hard to attribute.

ROR.name: ROR
ROR.short: RORA, RORB and RORC (RORalpha/beta/gamma) are nuclear receptors that bind DNA as monomers to the ROR response element, or RORE: an AGGTCA nuclear-receptor half-site preceded by a 5-6 bp AT-rich extension, most often written AAAGTAGGTCA. The extension is read by a C-terminal extension of the DNA-binding domain lying in the minor groove, and it is the only feature that distinguishes a RORE from the half-site shared by many other nuclear receptors. ROREs form the second transcriptional loop of the mammalian circadian clock, where RORs activate Bmal1 in competition with the REV-ERB repressors at the same sites. RORgammat, a thymus-restricted RORC isoform, drives the Th17 program and is a drug target in autoimmune disease.

NR2E.name: NR2E (TLX / PNR)
NR2E.short: NR2E is a small orphan nuclear-receptor group with two human members: NR2E1 (TLX, the homolog of Drosophila tailless) and NR2E3 (PNR, photoreceptor-specific nuclear receptor). Unusually for the superfamily, they prefer the hexamer AAGTCA rather than the AGGTCA half-site read by most nuclear receptors, a switch traced to a residue in the P-box of the recognition helix; the fuller models add a 5' A/T-rich extension and a tandem repeat of the core. The two factors are almost never co-expressed: TLX maintains neural stem and progenitor cells in the forebrain, while PNR acts in rod photoreceptors with CRX and NRL. NR2E3 mutations cause enhanced S-cone syndrome, a retinal cell-fate disorder.

ZNF_SCAN_OTHER.name: Thinly characterized small families
ZNF_SCAN_OTHER.short: This is not a motif family. It is a holding pen for small, thinly characterized factors that needed somewhere to go, and it currently holds eleven matrices for nine unrelated proteins: MSANTD1, MSANTD3 and MSANTD4, DNTTIP1, FLYWCH1, FAM200B, ELYS/AHCTF1, NACC2 and XPA. Internal cohesion is 0.47, the lowest of any group in this atlas. Two warnings about the label. The name mentions SCAN and SSX domains, but no SCAN-domain or SSX protein has a motif here; and BANP, named in the definition, is not here either - its only model sits in the other-BTB-zinc-finger bucket. XPA is the central scaffold of nucleotide excision repair, not a transcription factor. The motifs themselves are mostly well supported.

EBF.name: EBF / COE
EBF.short: EBF1-EBF4 (COE1-COE4, also Olf-1 and O/E-1 to O/E-3) bind a 10-base palindrome, TCCCNNGGGA, as homodimers. Despite being filed with the bHLH proteins, their DNA-binding domain is a pseudo-immunoglobulin fold structurally similar to the Rel homology domains of NF-κB and NFAT, contacting DNA through two loops and a unique zinc-coordination motif, with each subunit reaching across both half-sites; the HLH they carry is used for dimerisation, not DNA contact. EBF1 is required at the earliest committed step of B-lymphocyte development and shows pioneer-like activity on closed chromatin; EBF2 establishes brown adipocyte identity; de novo EBF3 variants cause a hypotonia-ataxia-developmental-delay syndrome. The motif is long enough that scans for it are relatively clean.

ESRR.name: Estrogen-related receptors
ESRR.short: The estrogen-related receptors ERRalpha (ESRRA), ERRbeta (ESRRB) and ERRgamma (ESRRG) are orphan nuclear receptors with no established natural ligand; their activity is set by coactivators such as PGC-1alpha rather than by a hormone. Unlike most nuclear receptors they bind DNA as monomers, on a single AGGTCA half-site carrying a three-base 5' extension: TNAAGGTCA, usually seen as TCAAGGTCA. The extension is read by a C-terminal extension of the DNA-binding domain in the minor groove, and it is what allows a monomer to bind with high affinity. The three paralogues share one motif and are not distinguishable from sequence. ERR sites sit at nuclear-encoded mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes, at pluripotency enhancers, and in the placenta and inner ear.

NR4A.name: NR4A (NUR77/NURR1)
NR4A.short: NR4A1 (NUR77), NR4A2 (NURR1) and NR4A3 (NOR-1) are orphan nuclear receptors and immediate-early genes: they are transcribed within minutes of serum stimulation, depolarization or antigen-receptor signaling and their proteins turn over quickly. Unlike most nuclear receptors they bind DNA as monomers, to a single AGGTCA half-site carried on an A/T-rich 5' extension, giving the eight-base NGFI-B response element AAAGGTCA. A separate protein surface, the A box, reads those A-T base pairs in the minor groove. The same receptors can also act as homodimers on the everted NurRE and as heterodimers with RXR. Because a monomeric half-site constrains only eight or nine positions, matches are common by chance, and the AGGTCA core is shared with most of the nuclear receptor superfamily.

REV_ERB.name: REV-ERB (NR1D)
REV_ERB.short: REV-ERBalpha (NR1D1) and REV-ERBbeta (NR1D2) are nuclear receptors that lack the helix-12 activation surface and act only as repressors, recruiting the NCoR-HDAC3 complex and binding heme as a ligand. They read the same DNA as the RORs: an AGGTCA half-site with a 5' AT-rich extension (the RORE, or RevRE), and preferentially a direct repeat of two such sites separated by 2 bp, called RevDR2, on which they bind as homodimers. Together with the RORs they form the second feedback loop of the mammalian circadian clock, alternately repressing and activating Bmal1 at the same sites. Loss of both paralogues disrupts circadian behavior and causes hepatic steatosis and metabolic derangement.

CTCF.name: CTCF
CTCF.short: CTCF is a single, near-ubiquitously expressed protein whose eleven C2H2 zinc fingers read an asymmetric, roughly 15-20 bp GC-rich sequence, often with a second recognition module a few bases upstream. Tens of thousands of these sites act as insulators and as anchors for cohesin-extruded chromatin loops, so they delimit topologically associating domains and separate enhancers from promoters they should not reach. Because the motif is long, information-rich, and read by a well-characterized finger-to-base code solved in two crystal structures, a CTCF match is one of the few motif hits that predicts real occupancy reasonably often. The site is directional: which strand it lies on determines which way a loop is anchored, and convergent pairs of sites are the ones that form loops.

ESR.name: Estrogen receptors
ESR.short: The estrogen receptors ERalpha (ESR1) and ERbeta (ESR2) are estradiol-activated nuclear receptors that bind DNA as homodimers on the estrogen response element, a 15 bp inverted repeat of the hexamer AGGTCA with a 3 bp spacer: AGGTCAnnnTGACCT, usually quoted as its 13 bp core GGTCAnnnTGACC. The element differs from the glucocorticoid-type half-site by only two base pairs, and the same 3 bp spacing and dimer geometry are shared with the steroid receptors, so the half-site sequence rather than the architecture is what marks it as estrogenic. ESR1 and ESR2 cannot be told apart by sequence. These sites drive the estrogen program in breast, uterus, bone and liver, and they are the regulatory target of tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors and fulvestrant.

NFY.name: NF-Y (CBF)
NFY.short: NF-Y is a heterotrimer of NFYA, NFYB and NFYC that binds the CCAAT box, one of the most frequent elements in eukaryotic promoters. NFYB and NFYC carry histone-fold domains and pair like H2A/H2B, gripping the DNA backbone and bending it; NFYA supplies the only sequence-specific contacts, inserting an alpha helix into the minor groove to read CCAAT. All three subunits are required for binding, so the three gene symbols describe one molecular entity and one motif. NF-Y is ubiquitous, sits at a fixed distance upstream of transcription start sites, and helps open chromatin for cell-type-specific factors. NF-YA is overexpressed and alternatively spliced in several cancers.

ZBED.name: BED-type zinc finger
ZBED.short: BED fingers are zinc-coordinating DNA-binding modules named for the two proteins in which they were first recognized, Drosophila BEAF and DREF, and they are shared with the hAT superfamily of DNA transposases. Vertebrate ZBED genes arose from at least two independent domestication events of hAT elements, so this is a second family of transposase recognition modules turned into host transcription factors. Nine motifs cover four proteins. Only ZBED1, the human DREF orthologue hDREF, has a strong and reproducible site: all four of its models converge on TATCGCGACAT, a relative of the Drosophila DNA replication-related element TATCGATA. ZBED2, ZBED4 and ZBED5 contribute short, weaker and partly conflicting models.

HD_HNF1.name: HNF1
HD_HNF1.short: HNF1A and HNF1B are the only two members of this family, and they bind an unusually long 13-bp near-palindrome, GTTAATNATTAAC, as an obligate dimer. Each subunit contributes an atypical homeodomain carrying a 21-residue insertion, paired with a POU-specific-like domain that was only recognized once the protein-DNA structure was solved. Because the dimer is rigid, the spacing between the two half-sites is fixed and the resulting motif carries about 15-16 bits of information - among the most specific sites of any homeodomain-related family. The two factors drive liver, pancreatic islet, kidney tubule and intestinal gene expression, and heterozygous loss of either causes a distinct form of monogenic diabetes (MODY3 for HNF1A, MODY5 with renal cysts for HNF1B).

GFI.name: GFI1 / GFI1B
GFI.short: GFI1 and GFI1B are six-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger repressors of blood cell development that bind a well-defined AATC-core site, TAAATCAC(A/T)GC. Only fingers 3, 4 and 5 make the sequence-specific contacts; repression comes from the N-terminal SNAG peptide, which docks into LSD1 and pulls in the LSD1/CoREST complex. GFI1 acts in granulocyte, T-cell and hematopoietic stem cell programs, GFI1B in erythroid and megakaryocyte programs, and the two proteins bind indistinguishable sequences, so a motif hit identifies the pair rather than one member. Dominant-negative GFI1 mutations cause severe congenital neutropenia; dominant-negative GFI1B mutations cause gray platelet syndrome. The site is AT-rich, information-dense and unusually specific for a C2H2 motif.

ZNF143.name: ZNF143 / THAP11 (SBS)
ZNF143.short: The SPH element, also called the SBS, is a promoter element read by three proteins that are not close relatives. ZNF143 (originally Staf) and its paralogue ZNF76 are C2H2 zinc-finger activators; THAP11 (Ronin) uses an unrelated THAP zinc-coordinating domain and occupies the same sequence in a complex with the coactivator HCFC1. The site sits close to transcription start sites at thousands of CpG-island promoters, where it drives small nuclear RNA genes transcribed by RNA polymerase II and III and a large set of protein-coding genes, prominently nuclear-encoded mitochondrial and ribosomal ones. The element was once presented as a sequence-specific anchor for chromatin loops; that role has since been retracted, but its promoter activity is well supported.

OVOL.name: OVOL (OVO-like)
OVOL.short: OVOL1 and OVOL2 are C2H2 zinc-finger repressors, the mammalian counterparts of Drosophila OVO/shavenbaby, that bind a short AT-flanked core, CCGTTA (equivalently TAACGG on the other strand). They act mainly as repressors of the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, holding epithelial cells in an epithelial state by shutting down ZEB1, ZEB2 and other EMT inducers, and OVOL1 additionally represses its own promoter and MYC. Mouse knockouts show defects in hair follicles, sperm, kidney, mammary ductal morphogenesis and epidermal progenitor arrest. In humans, a promoter point mutation that mis-expresses OVOL2 in corneal endothelium causes posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy type 1. OVOL1 and OVOL2 share one motif and cannot be separated from sequence.

USF.name: USF
USF.short: USF1 and USF2 are ubiquitously expressed bHLH-LZ proteins, first purified as the adenovirus major late transcription factor (MLTF), that bind DNA as homodimers and heterodimers. They read a canonical E-box core, but with a characteristic extended palindromic preference, GTCACGTGAC: the T and A flanks are what separate a USF site from a MYC-MAX site, which prefers C and G there. Because both proteins are constitutive, USF motifs turn up in a very large number of accessible promoters and CpG islands in every cell type, making USF one of the most frequently recovered motifs in promoter and footprint analyses. Human genetics links USF1 variants to familial combined hyperlipidemia.

ARID.name: ARID / BRIGHT
ARID.short: ARID stands for AT-rich interaction domain, and this family is restricted to the four human ARID proteins that really do read AT-rich sequence: ARID3A (Bright), ARID3B, ARID5A and ARID5B. Eight motifs converge on a five to eight base-pair AT core - ATTAAT for ARID3B, ATTAAA for ARID3A, AATATT for ARID5A - so the whole family occupies one narrow, information-poor patch of sequence space and is very hard to separate from homeodomain TAAT sites or from AT-rich DNA generally. The many other ARID-domain proteins, including ARID1A and ARID1B in BAF and ARID2 in PBAF, bind DNA without sequence preference and are deliberately excluded from this family.

HD_DUX.name: DUX / DUXA
HD_DUX.short: DUX4 and its relatives DUXA and DUXB carry two homeodomains in tandem within a single polypeptide, an architecture found only in placental mammals and derived from a retrotransposed copy of an ancestral homeobox gene. The two domains bind side by side, head to head, and together read an eleven-base site, TAATCTAATCA, that is far longer and more specific than a single homeodomain site. These genes are normally expressed only for a few cell divisions after fertilisation, where they help switch on the embryonic genome and a set of endogenous retroviral promoters. Misexpression of DUX4 in skeletal muscle causes facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, and DUX4 rearrangements define a subtype of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, so this motif marks one of the better understood pathogenic regulatory programs.

MAZ.name: MAZ / PATZ1
MAZ.short: MAZ, the Myc-associated zinc finger protein, and PATZ1 are broadly expressed C2H2 zinc-finger proteins that bind short G-rich runs, written GGGAGGG or GGGGAGGGG and read as CCCTCCCC on the opposite strand. MAZ was cloned as the protein binding ME1a1, an element between the c-MYC P1 and P2 promoters. Interest in the motif increased when MAZ turned out to be a second insulator-type element: it colocalizes with CTCF at chromatin boundaries, contacts the cohesin subunit RAD21, and deleting MAZ motifs at the Hox clusters disrupts boundaries much as deleting CTCF motifs does. The single-base difference from the SP1 GC-box, an A where the GC-box has a C, is the only sequence discriminator, and it is thin.

HIC.name: HIC1 / HIC2
HIC.short: HIC1 (hypermethylated in cancer 1) and HIC2 are BTB/POZ zinc-finger repressors with five Kruppel-like C2H2 fingers. Their optimal site, defined by site selection, is (C/G)NG(C/G)GGGCA(C/A)CC, with a GGCA core read by fingers 3 and 4; databases usually render the same element on the opposite strand as TGCC(A/G), which is why the family is often listed with a short TGCC consensus. The BTB domain blocks binding to a single site but supports cooperative binding to several, so genuine targets carry multiple sites. HIC1 sits at 17p13.3, is induced by p53, is frequently silenced by promoter hypermethylation in tumors, and represses SIRT1; heterozygous mouse mutants develop tumors.

IKZF.name: IKZF (Ikaros)
IKZF.short: The Ikaros family (IKZF1 Ikaros, IKZF2 Helios, IKZF3 Aiolos, IKZF4 Eos, IKZF5 Pegasus) are lymphoid zinc-finger proteins with an N-terminal C2H2 array that binds DNA and a C-terminal pair of fingers that mediates homo- and heterodimerization. They recognize a GGGAA core, present in lymphocyte-specific regulatory elements and also in pericentromeric satellite repeats, to which Ikaros localizes by direct DNA binding.
