IKZF1 is required for the development of all lymphoid lineages, is deleted in BCR-ABL1 and Ph-like B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia where it predicts poor outcome, and, with IKZF3, is the protein whose thalidomide-analog-induced degradation explains how lenalidomide works in myeloma. The GGGAA core is shared with ETS and NF-kB sites, which makes these motifs hard to trust.

BCL11.name: BCL11A / BCL11B
BCL11.short: BCL11A and BCL11B (originally CTIP1 and CTIP2) are paralogous C2H2 zinc-finger repressors with six fingers, of which a C-terminal cluster binds DNA while the N-terminal region recruits NuRD. They are best known not as motif proteins but as switches: BCL11A silences the fetal gamma-globin genes and is the target of approved gene-editing therapies for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, while BCL11B enforces T-lineage commitment, so that its loss converts T cells into natural-killer-like cells. Reported DNA preferences conflict. In vitro selection on BCL11A gave a GC-box-like GGCCGG core, whereas the site it occupies at the gamma-globin promoter is written TGACCA. The family's matrices are heterogeneous and several look like other factors' motifs.

ZNF460.name: ZNF460 / ZNF317-like
ZNF460.short: ZNF460 and ZNF317 are poorly characterized human C2H2 zinc-finger proteins grouped here because their database motifs cluster together, not because a published experiment showed they read the same sequence. The family is the least coherent in this part of the atlas: its eight matrices split into two unrelated groups, one a long AGTCTGCTGT-type word from ZNF317 in vitro data and the other a GC-rich GCCTCAGCCTCCC-type word from ZNF460 that closely resembles Alu consensus sequence. No single consensus is given here because the data do not support one. Almost everything known about either protein comes from high-throughput surveys of zinc-finger binding specificity rather than from focused study.

HINFP.name: HINFP (MIZF)
HINFP.short: HINFP, also called HiNF-P and originally cloned as MIZF, is a seven-finger C2H2 zinc-finger protein that reads a short CGGAC core, usually written CGGACGTT. Its best-characterized job is at the replication-dependent histone H4 genes, where it binds a conserved cell-cycle element in the proximal promoter and, using the cyclin E/CDK2 substrate NPAT/p220 as coactivator, switches on H4 transcription at the G1-to-S transition. It is the endpoint of a linear pathway from growth-factor-induced cyclin E/CDK2 activity to histone synthesis. The same protein was independently identified as a partner of the methyl-CpG-binding protein MBD2 and acts as a repressor in that context, so the motif can mean activation or repression depending on the promoter.

GCM.name: GCM (glial cells missing)
GCM.short: GCM1 and GCM2 (glial cells missing 1 and 2) are the only human members of a small metazoan family that binds DNA through the GCM domain, a conserved 150-residue region with a fold unlike any other transcription factor class: two subdomains held together by structural zinc ions, reading the major groove with a five-stranded beta-sheet rather than an alpha-helix. They recognize an 8-bp GCM box, AT(G/A)CGGGT, as monomers, with no half-sites or spacing rules. Despite the name, the mammalian proteins are not gliogenic: GCM1 is required for placental labyrinth branching and trophoblast fusion, and GCM2 for parathyroid gland development, where loss-of-function and activating mutations cause hypoparathyroidism and hyperparathyroidism respectively.

PLAG.name: PLAG / PLAGL
PLAG.short: The PLAG proteins - PLAG1, PLAGL1 (also called ZAC1 or LOT1) and PLAGL2 - are C2H2 zinc-finger factors with seven fingers that read a bipartite G-rich site: a GRGGC core and a GGG cluster separated by roughly six to eight base pairs. Finger 3 contacts the G-cluster and fingers 6 and 7 contact the core, so the two halves are read by different parts of one protein. PLAG1 is the classic translocation target in salivary-gland pleomorphic adenoma, where promoter swapping with CTNNB1 or LIFR switches it on; PLAGL2 is also transforming, while PLAGL1/ZAC1 is an imprinted, maternally silenced growth suppressor whose loss of imprinting causes transient neonatal diabetes. All three activate IGF2.

OSR.name: OSR1 / OSR2
OSR.short: OSR1 and OSR2 (odd-skipped related 1 and 2) are the two vertebrate members of the Odd family of C2H2 zinc-finger proteins, homologs of Drosophila odd-skipped. OSR1 carries three tandem C2H2 fingers and OSR2 five, and both bind the 8-mer GCTACTGT, established by in vitro selection. Despite the C2H2 class label, this motif is not GC-rich — the central TACTG carries most of the information. Both proteins are mesenchymal and developmentally restricted: OSR1 is required for the metanephric mesenchyme and hence for kidney formation, OSR2 for palatal shelf growth, and loss of either causes a distinct mouse malformation. A knock-in experiment showed the two coding sequences are functionally interchangeable, so their different phenotypes reflect where they are expressed rather than what they bind.

RBP_INFERRED.name: RNA-binding proteins with inferred DNA motifs
aka: RNA-binding proteins with inferred DNA motifs
RBP motifs in a DNA motif database
RBP_INFERRED.short: This is not a motif family. It is a warning label. The factors here have motifs that came out of RNA-binding proteins run through DNA assays, or out of inference, so the matrices filed under their names should be read with real caution. Three proteins are present - CPEB1, LIN28B and MBNL2, plus a generic MBNL archetype - across eight models, at cohesion 0.50. All three are bona fide RNA-binding proteins with well-mapped RNA elements, and for CPEB1 the DNA matrix is simply that RNA element with T written for U: its models read TTTTAT and AATAAAA, the cytoplasmic polyadenylation element and its own reverse complement. Scanning genomic DNA against these is usually a mistake. Read the RNA literature instead, and look up the RNA motif.

TAL_LYL.name: TAL1 / LYL1 (hematopoietic)
TAL_LYL.short: TAL1 (SCL), LYL1 and TAL2 are haematopoietic and endothelial class II basic helix-loop-helix proteins with no intrinsic DNA-binding activity: they bind only as heterodimers with the class I E-proteins E12/E47, TCF4 or TCF12. In blood cells the functional unit is larger still — a pentameric complex in which LMO2 bridges the TAL1-E47 dimer to GATA1 or GATA2 with LDB1 — and it reads a composite element made of an E-box followed about nine base pairs later by a GATA site. TAL1 is required for all primitive haematopoiesis and is the most frequently activated oncogene in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. The family is the atlas's clearest example of a motif that is really a composite, and partly a partner's.

BHLHE40_41.name: BHLHE40 / BHLHE41 (DEC1/2)
BHLHE40_41.short: BHLHE40 and BHLHE41 - also known as DEC1/STRA13/SHARP-2 and DEC2/SHARP-1 - are bHLH repressors without a leucine zipper that bind the class-B E-box CACGTG and shut down transcription, both by competing for E-boxes with activating dimers such as CLOCK-BMAL1 and by recruiting histone deacetylases without contacting DNA. Their own promoters carry hypoxia response elements, so they couple HIF signalling to the E-box landscape. A BHLHE41 missense change causes familial natural short sleep in humans and mice, BHLHE40 is required for pathogenic T cell cytokine output, and the two together control alveolar macrophage identity. Because they read the same site as circadian activators, the sequence alone cannot tell you whether an E-box is being activated or repressed.

BCL6.name: BCL6 / BCL6B
BCL6.short: BCL6 and its paralogue BCL6B (BAZF) are BTB/POZ zinc-finger repressors that bind a nine-base site, TTCCTAGAA, which is a TTCNNNGAA element of the same class that STAT dimers use. That overlap is not incidental: BCL6 represses interleukin-4-induced, STAT6-dependent genes by occupying sites that STAT6 would otherwise use, so the same sequence can be an activating STAT element or a repressed BCL6 element depending on which protein is present. BCL6 is required for germinal center formation and for follicular helper T cells, and its deregulation by chromosomal translocation or promoter mutation occurs in a large fraction of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas. A hit to this motif is ambiguous between BCL6, BCL6B and the STAT family.

DACH.name: DACH / SKI-family corepressors
DACH.short: These are transcriptional corepressors, not classical sequence-specific activators. DACH1 and DACH2 are the vertebrate Dachshund proteins, and SKI, SKIL/SnoN, SKOR1 and SKOR2 are the Ski family; all share a Dachshund homology domain with a winged-helix fold related to forkhead. They work mostly by being recruited: DACH proteins into SIX/EYA complexes and onto forkhead sites where they compete with FOXM1, the Ski proteins onto SMAD complexes to shut down TGF-beta signalling, and SKOR1/SKOR2 onto homeodomain factors such as LBX1. The motifs in this family therefore look borrowed. The best-supported models, TTAATTAC for SKOR1 and SKOR2, are indistinguishable from homeodomain dimer sites, which is what you would expect from proteins that arrive at DNA on someone else's back.

TFAP4.name: TFAP4 (AP-4)
TFAP4.short: TFAP4 (AP-4) is a single-gene bHLH-LZ family with no close paralogue. Unusually for the class, a second zipper-like dimerization motif restricts it to homodimers, so it does not form the combinatorial heterodimers that dominate the rest of the bHLH class. It binds the palindromic class-A E-box CAGCTG, usually written extended as AACAGCTGAT. TFAP4 is a direct MYC target and represses the CDK inhibitor CDKN1A (p21), placing it in a MYC-driven cell-cycle circuit whose direction is context-dependent - growth-promoting in several carcinomas, tumour-suppressive in B lymphocytes. Because CAGCTG is shared with the E-proteins and with most tissue-restricted bHLH factors, a match is weak evidence for AP-4 specifically.

NR5A.name: NR5A (SF-1 / LRH-1)
NR5A.short: NR5A1 (steroidogenic factor 1, SF-1) and NR5A2 (liver receptor homolog 1, LRH-1) are the mammalian relatives of Drosophila FTZ-F1. Like the NR4A receptors they bind DNA as monomers rather than dimers, occupying one AGGTCA half-site plus a short 5' extension read by a separate protein surface called the A box, which gives the nine-base SF-1 response element TCAAGGTCA. NR5A1 drives adrenal and gonadal development and the steroidogenic enzyme genes; NR5A2 works in liver, pancreas, intestine and the early embryo. The two proteins have indistinguishable motifs but almost non-overlapping tissue distributions, so cell type, not sequence, tells them apart. The element differs from the NR4A site at a single base and is contained inside the NR6A1 direct repeat.

NR6A1.name: NR6A1 (GCNF)
NR6A1.short: NR6A1, better known as germ cell nuclear factor (GCNF), is the only mammalian member of nuclear receptor subfamily 6: one gene with no paralogue. It binds a DR0, two nuclear receptor half-sites in direct repeat with no intervening bases, and it does so as a homodimer without an RXR partner. That makes it the odd one out among the orphan receptors here, because a two-half-site element of 13 to 15 base pairs is far more specific than a monomeric half-site. Its best-characterized job is repressing the pluripotency gene Oct4 during differentiation, which it does by recruiting methyl-CpG-binding proteins and DNA methyltransferases. Mouse mutants show posterior truncation, the gene underlies a vertebral-number locus in pigs, and human variants cause an oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome.

THAP.name: THAP-type zinc finger
THAP.short: THAP-type zinc fingers are C2CH modules whose closest known relative is the site-specific DNA-binding domain of the Drosophila P-element transposase, making this a family of domesticated transposase DNA-binding domains. The atlas files six motifs for two proteins, THAP1 and THAP12. THAP1 recognizes a bipartite site - a GCCATCTT-like half and a GGGCA half separated by a short variable spacer - which the trimmed JASPAR model reduces to GCAGGGCA. Crystallography of the fly THAP domain explains the bipartite pattern: a beta-sheet inserts into the major groove while a basic C-terminal loop reads the adjacent minor groove. THAP1 is the DYT6 dystonia gene. THAP11 is deliberately not filed here; it shares the ZNF143 SBS element and is covered by the ZNF143 entry.

ZNF263.name: ZNF263
ZNF263.short: ZNF263 is a nine-finger C2H2 zinc-finger protein that also carries a KRAB repression domain and a SCAN oligomerization domain. Its binding site is unusually long: genome-wide mapping in K562 cells recovered a roughly 24-nucleotide GA-rich element built from tandem GGAGGA-like units, which differs in several positions from what the zinc-finger recognition code predicted for this protein. Unlike most KRAB zinc-finger proteins it does not sit mainly on transposable elements, and many of its thousands of target sites lie inside transcribed regions rather than at promoters; knockdown both raises and lowers target genes. The GA-rich character makes this motif easy to confuse with purine-rich sites read by ETS and SP1-like factors on the opposite strand.

ZNF281.name: ZNF281 / ZNF148 (ZBP-89)
ZNF281.short: ZNF148 (better known as ZBP-89) and ZNF281 (ZBP-99) are broadly expressed four-fingered C2H2 proteins that bind GC- and GA-rich promoter elements, most often written GGGGGAGGGG or, on the opposite strand, CCCCTCCCCC; longer models add a CCCCACCCC module. Both were cloned as factors that occupy GC-rich elements already known to bind Sp1, and that competition is the point: the same element is a legitimate site for several families. ZNF219 is grouped with them on domain similarity but has no matrix here. The two proteins are not distinguishable from each other by sequence, and only weakly distinguishable from MAZ, PATZ1 and VEZF1. Human ZNF148 truncating variants cause a recognized developmental syndrome.

ZFP_TE.name: Transposase-derived / TE-binding zinc fingers
ZFP_TE.short: A small entry for KRAB zinc fingers whose recognized sequence is itself a piece of a transposable element. The best-documented cases are ZNF91, which binds the VNTR region of SVA elements, and ZNF93, which binds a segment of the 5' untranslated region of primate L1 retrotransposons. Both changed as those element families began to spread, and the L1PA3 subfamily escaped ZNF93 by deleting its binding site. The atlas holds six matrices for three proteins, ZNF93, ZNF808 and ZNF780A; ZNF91 itself has no motif in any of the four source databases. Because these motifs are copies of element sequence rather than compact regulatory words, a match usually tells you which repeat you are inside rather than which protein is bound there.

AHR.name: AHR / AHRR
AHR.short: The xenobiotic response element is the site bound by the aryl hydrocarbon receptor, AHR, paired with ARNT. Both are bHLH-PAS proteins. AHR sits in the cytoplasm in a complex with HSP90 and XAP2 until it binds a ligand: dioxins and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, or endogenous tryptophan metabolites such as kynurenine. It then enters the nucleus, exchanges its chaperones for ARNT, and binds an asymmetric half-site pair in which AHR reads the 5' TNGC and ARNT reads the 3' GTG, giving the core TNGCGTG. The paralogue AHRR is induced by AHR and represses it by competing for ARNT and for the same element. Occupied sites drive the cytochrome P450 genes CYP1A1, CYP1A2 and CYP1B1, so this motif is the entry point of the classical xenobiotic-metabolism response.

TBP.name: TBP / TATA
TBP.short: The TATA box is the oldest known eukaryotic core promoter element and the binding site of TBP, the TATA-box-binding protein. TBP is a saddle-shaped, internally pseudo-symmetric protein that straddles about eight base pairs of AT-rich DNA, reads them entirely from the minor groove, kinks the duplex at both ends and bends it by roughly 80 degrees. It works within TFIID for RNA polymerase II and within SL1 and TFIIIB for polymerases I and III, so a single protein serves all three. Because minor-groove contacts barely distinguish A:T from T:A, the element carries little information: the canonical TATAWAWR is present in only a small minority of human promoters, most of which are instead GC-rich and TATA-less. A TATA match on its own is therefore very weak evidence of anything.

WT1.name: WT1
WT1.short: WT1 is the Wilms tumor suppressor, a four-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger protein whose last three fingers are closely related to those of EGR1 and which binds essentially the same GC-rich site. In vitro selection also found a slightly different high-affinity site, GCGTGGGAGT, called the WTE. Alternative splicing inserts three amino acids (lysine-threonine-serine) between fingers three and four, and the +KTS form binds DNA poorly but binds RNA and localizes to splicing-factor compartments, so WT1 is a DNA-binding protein only in part. Expression is restricted to developing kidney and gonad, podocytes, mesothelium and epicardium. The WT1 matrices in motif databases are ChIP-derived and G-rich rather than EGR-like, which matters when reading a hit.

ZEB.name: ZEB
ZEB.short: ZEB1 and ZEB2 are large C2H2 zinc-finger repressors that bind the E-box-like sequence CACCTG, written CAGGTG when read on the other strand. Each protein carries two widely separated zinc-finger clusters, either of which can engage a site, so one molecule can hold two boxes at once. ZEB proteins contain no basic helix-loop-helix domain, yet they compete for the same CAGGTG boxes that bHLH activators use, so an E-box hit does not imply a bHLH factor. Both paralogues repress epithelial genes, E-cadherin (CDH1) above all, and are central to epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Loss-of-function mutations cause posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy (ZEB1) and Mowat-Wilson syndrome (ZEB2), and high ZEB1 marks poorly differentiated carcinomas.

ZNF384.name: ZNF384 / ZNF362
ZNF384.short: ZNF384 and its near-identical paralogue ZNF362 are C2H2 zinc-finger proteins that bind homopolymeric runs of A on one strand and T on the other. They are unusual among zinc fingers in reading the minor groove of an A-tract rather than the major groove of a mixed sequence, and only three of their fingers contact DNA. ZNF384 was cloned twice, as CIZ, a partner of the adaptor p130Cas that activates matrix metalloproteinase genes, and as Nmp4, a nuclear matrix factor at the type I collagen alpha-1 promoter. In human leukaemia ZNF384 is a recurrent fusion partner: rearrangements joining its C-terminal region to EP300, TCF3, TAF15 and others define a subtype of B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.

ZNF768.name: ZNF768
ZNF768.short: ZNF768 is a C2H2 zinc-finger protein whose binding site sits in the core region of mammalian-wide interspersed repeats (MIRs), an old family of SINE retrotransposons. The site is bipartite: GCTGTGTG and CCTCTCTG separated by about twenty unconstrained bases, so the two halves are usually reported separately and most motif databases hold only one of them. ZNF768 binding is concentrated in euchromatin and at promoters of expressed genes, and its own N-terminus contains a heptad repeat array structurally reminiscent of the RNA polymerase II C-terminal domain, which is where the frequent comparison to MYC-box-like repeats comes from. The literature is recent and small: two primary characterizations plus mouse work linking it to RAS-induced senescence and p53.

MTF1.name: MTF1
MTF1.short: MTF1 (MTF-1) is a six-finger C2H2 zinc-finger protein that binds the metal response element, a short TGCRCNC core first defined as the 12-base-pair repeat that makes metallothionein promoters metal-inducible. MTF1 is constitutively present but only becomes an activator when free zinc rises, so the same site is quiet in resting cells and strongly occupied after exposure to zinc, cadmium, copper or other heavy metals, and under oxidative and hypoxic stress. Metallothionein promoters carry several MREs in tandem, and that clustering, rather than any single site, is what produces a large induction. Mouse Mtf1 knockout is embryonic-lethal with liver degeneration. Because the core is only seven informative bases, isolated genomic matches are common and mostly meaningless.

ZFP57.name: ZFP57 / imprinting
ZFP57.short: ZFP57 is a KRAB zinc-finger protein that reads a six-base sequence, TGCCGC, but only when the CpG inside it is methylated. That combination of a short site and a methylation requirement lets it mark the methylated parental allele at imprinting control regions, the germline-methylated switches that restrict about two dozen loci to expression from one parent's chromosome. ZFP57 binds together with the corepressor TRIM28/KAP1 and DNA methyltransferases, shielding those regions from the wave of demethylation that follows fertilization. The larger zinc finger ZNF445 reads the same element and covers most of the same regions, which is why loss of ZFP57 alone produces imprinting defects with incomplete penetrance. In humans, recessive ZFP57 mutations cause transient neonatal diabetes with hypomethylation at multiple imprinted loci.

TELOBOX.name: Telobox (TERF1/TERF2/ZBTB48)
TELOBOX.short: The telobox factors TERF1 (TRF1) and TERF2 (TRF2) bind the vertebrate telomeric repeat TTAGGG through a single Myb-type helix-turn-helix domain that is, structurally, a homeodomain-like fold. Both work as preformed homodimers, and the dimer reads two YTAGGGTTR half-sites whose spacing and orientation are almost unconstrained, so the footprint on a tandem repeat array is flexible rather than fixed. ZBTB48 (TZAP) is a zinc-finger protein that binds the same telomeric and subtelomeric variant repeats and triggers telomere trimming. Because the motif is the telomeric repeat itself, a match in the genome is almost always either a true telomere, a subtelomeric region, or an interstitial telomeric sequence - not a conventional regulatory element.

SRF.name: SRF
SRF.short: The CArG box is the site of a single protein, serum response factor, which binds as a homodimer through a MADS box - the same fold MEF2 uses, reading a different sequence. The element is CC(A/T)6GG: a ten-base near-palindrome in which the outer CC and GG carry the specificity and the six central A/T positions are effectively free, giving a well-defined but degenerate site. SRF is expressed almost everywhere and is constitutively bound to many of its sites; what changes with signalling is not occupancy but which coactivator family it recruits - the ETS-domain TCF proteins downstream of MAP kinase, or the actin-regulated MRTF proteins downstream of Rho. Both bind the same CArG box, so the motif does not tell you which programme is running.

CSL.name: CSL / RBPJ
CSL.short: CSL is the DNA-binding transcription factor at the end of the Notch pathway, named for its three orthologues: CBF1/RBPJ in mammals, Suppressor of Hairless in Drosophila and LAG-1 in C. elegans. Humans have one broadly expressed gene, RBPJ, plus the pancreas-restricted paralogue RBPJL. RBPJ binds the seven-base element GTGGGAA, often written on the other strand as TTCCCAC, and does so whether or not Notch is active: without a Notch intracellular domain it recruits corepressors, and with one it assembles an activating ternary complex with Mastermind-like coactivators. Some Notch targets carry two sites in a head-to-head pair with fixed spacing, an SPS, which allows two Notch complexes to dimerize. Notch signaling through RBPJ controls lateral inhibition, T-cell specification and vascular development, and is constitutively activated in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

PROSPERO.name: PROX1 (Prospero)
PROSPERO.short: PROX1 is the human counterpart of Drosophila Prospero, and it binds DNA with a module unlike any other homeodomain: a highly divergent homeodomain fused to a conserved Prospero domain, the two folding into one structural unit called the homeo-prospero domain. That unit reads a non-canonical site, TAAGACG, rather than the TAAT core used by ordinary homeodomains, and the Prospero domain both aligns the protein on DNA and masks a nuclear export signal, coupling DNA binding to where the protein sits in the cell. PROX1 is essential for lymphatic endothelium, lens fibre elongation, liver and pancreas development and dentate gyrus identity, and it also works without its own site by tethering to nuclear receptors. A single human gene, so no paralogue ambiguity.

HMG_OTHER.name: Other HMG-box
HMG_OTHER.short: This entry holds the HMG-box factors that are neither SOX nor TCF/LEF: HMG20A (iBRAF), HMG20B (BRAF35) and BBX (bobby sox homolog). They share only the fold. HMG20A and HMG20B are paralogous subunits of chromatin complexes - HMG20B of the LSD1-CoREST-HDAC complex that keeps neuronal genes off in non-neuronal cells, HMG20A of KMT2A/MLL complexes that turn them on - so their genomic distribution is largely set by whichever partner recruits the complex. BBX is a poorly characterized protein that groups phylogenetically with CIC rather than with SOX. The three measured motifs are unrelated to each other and to the SOX core, and this is the least coherent family in the HMG class; a hit here should be treated as a lead, not an identification.

REST.name: REST (NRSF)
REST.short: REST, also called NRSF, is a single zinc-finger protein that recognizes RE1 (the neuron- restrictive silencer element), a 21-base-pair site that is one of the longest and most information- rich transcription-factor motifs in the human genome. Eight of its nine zinc fingers read two half-sites separated by a two-base spacer, which is why the element is long and unusually specific. REST recruits SIN3-HDAC and CoREST-LSD1 complexes to silence neuronal genes in non-neuronal cells, and is removed or degraded as neurons differentiate. Human and mouse genomes contain roughly one to two thousand canonical RE1s, many spread by transposable elements, plus a larger set of weaker non-canonical variants. Unusually for a PWM, a strong RE1 match is good evidence of real REST binding.

ZBTB33.name: ZBTB33 (Kaiso)
ZBTB33.short: ZBTB33, better known as Kaiso, is a BTB/POZ zinc-finger repressor with only three C2H2 fingers and two distinct ways of reading DNA. It binds the non-methylated consensus TCCTGCNA - the Kaiso binding site, or KBS, whose minimal core is CTGCNA - and, separately, methylated CpG dinucleotides, with higher affinity for the KBS of the two. Crystal structures show both modes use the same first two fingers, with methylcytosine read through CH-to-O hydrogen bonds. Kaiso was found as a partner of p120-catenin, which blocks its DNA binding, and it links adhesion to transcription. Note that all four database matrices for ZBTB33 describe a CGCG-containing palindrome, TCTCGCGAGA, not the KBS.

MECOM.name: MECOM / EVI1
MECOM.short: MECOM, better known as EVI1, is a 145-kDa C2H2 zinc-finger protein with two separate finger clusters that bind two different sequences. The N-terminal cluster of seven fingers reads a 15-bp GATA-like site, GA(C/T)AAGA(T/C)AAGATAA, whose core is GACAAGATA; the C-terminal cluster of three fingers reads the unrelated GAAGATGAG. EVI1 is normally expressed in hematopoietic stem cells, kidney and lung, and is silenced in most differentiated blood cells. It is one of the strongest adverse prognostic markers in acute myeloid leukemia, where 3q26 rearrangements such as inv(3)(q21q26) do not create a fusion protein but move a GATA2 enhancer next to MECOM, switching the gene on. Germline MECOM mutations cause radioulnar synostosis with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia.

ZFX.name: ZFX / ZFY
ZFX.short: ZFX and its Y-linked paralogue ZFY are thirteen-finger C2H2 zinc-finger activators that bind a short GC-rich site containing a GGCCT core. Their placement is the interesting part: they bind inside CpG-island promoters a couple of hundred base pairs downstream of the transcription start site, between the open region at the TSS and the first downstream nucleosome, and they activate the promoters they occupy. Together with the related ZNF711, they occupy the majority of active CpG-island promoters in a cell. ZFX loss slows proliferation, which is why the gene recurs in growth-based CRISPR screens, and ZFX supports embryonic and hematopoietic stem-cell self-renewal. Germline ZFX variants cause an X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder.

ZNF410.name: ZNF410
ZNF410.short: ZNF410 is a five-finger C2H2 zinc-finger protein that recognizes a long, information-rich element, and it is the clearest known case of a mammalian transcription factor with essentially one target gene. Two conserved clusters near CHD4, which encodes the ATPase of the NuRD chromatin remodeling complex, together carry 27 copies of the motif; comparable clusters occur nowhere else in the genome. Removing ZNF410 lowers CHD4 protein by about 60 percent, which is enough to de-repress the fetal haemoglobin genes without obvious toxicity, and the factor was found in CRISPR screens for fetal haemoglobin silencers. Matches to the motif are therefore biologically meaningful mainly when they fall in those clusters, and isolated hits elsewhere rarely correspond to occupied, functional sites.

VEZF1.name: VEZF1
VEZF1.short: VEZF1, originally cloned twice as DB1 and as Vezf1, is a broadly expressed six-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger protein first defined on CT/GC-rich promoter elements and on the chicken beta-globin HS4 insulator, where its sites protect against DNA methylation. It has no established consensus sequence: the matrices in motif databases reduce either to a plain poly-C/poly-G run (JASPAR MA1578.2 is six positions long) or to GGGGGAGGGGG, which is the MAZ motif. That is the central problem with this family - the data cannot separate it from MAZ, PATZ1, ZNF281 or ZNF148. Its documented functions are in vascular development, in maintaining DNA methylation levels through Dnmt3b, and in slowing elongating RNA polymerase II.

NRF1.name: NRF1
NRF1.short: NRF1 (nuclear respiratory factor 1, also alpha-PAL) is a single-gene family whose DNA-binding domain belongs to no common fold class, its closest relatives being sea urchin P3A2 and Drosophila Erect wing. It binds as a homodimer to a palindrome, GCGCATGCGC, with each subunit contacting one GCGC half; motif models extend this to TGCGCATGCGC. The site contains two CpG dinucleotides in its most informative positions, so it is strongly associated with CpG-island promoters and is blocked by cytosine methylation. NRF1 sites sit in promoters of nuclear genes for mitochondrial proteins, including cytochrome c, cytochrome c oxidase subunits and TFAM, making NRF1 the main nuclear coordinator of mitochondrial biogenesis. It should not be confused with NFE2L1, also abbreviated Nrf1.

NPAS.name: NPAS3 / NPAS4 / other PAS
NPAS.short: NPAS3 and NPAS4 are neuronal bHLH-PAS transcription factors, relatives of CLOCK, HIF and AHR that heterodimerize with the same shared beta subunits ARNT and ARNT2 and read E-box-like sites built around a CGTG core. NPAS4 is an immediate-early gene induced by neuronal activity rather than by growth factors, and it controls the number of inhibitory synapses formed on excitatory neurons. NPAS3 is a broader brain factor whose disruption segregates with schizophrenia in one family. This is the thinnest family in the group: only three motif models exist, all derived from chromatin immunoprecipitation, and the NPAS4 and NPAS3 models do not actually resemble each other. A match here is best treated as a generic E-box variant unless neuronal, activity-dependent evidence supports more.

BHLH_OTHER.name: Other bHLH
BHLH_OTHER.short: A residual bucket rather than a real family: it holds bHLH motifs that could not be placed in any of the defined bHLH families. In the current release that is three models, all labelled SOHLH2, a germ-cell-restricted bHLH protein that heterodimerizes with SOHLH1 and controls spermatogonial differentiation and early folliculogenesis in mice. All three read an ordinary class-B E-box with a G/C flank (CACGTGC), and the data flags each one as resembling MYC/MAX or BHLHE40/41 motifs instead. The family definition also reserves space for MYRF-like factors and unclassified E-box archetypes, though none are assigned here. A hit means "canonical E-box", not SOHLH2.

NDT80.name: Ndt80/PhoG-like (C11orf9/MYRF)
NDT80.short: This family is named after the budding yeast meiotic activator Ndt80, whose DNA-binding domain defines an immunoglobulin-like fold shared by the human proteins MYRF and MYRFL. MYRF, myelin regulatory factor, is the only well-characterized vertebrate member. It is an endoplasmic-reticulum membrane protein that trimerizes and cleaves itself using a domain related to bacteriophage tailspike proteins; the released N-terminal fragment enters the nucleus and binds DNA. The measured site is the palindromic eight-base TGGTACCA, consistent with binding by a symmetric oligomer. MYRF is required for oligodendrocyte differentiation and for making and maintaining central nervous system myelin, and human MYRF variants cause a cardiac-urogenital syndrome and disorders of sex development.

HMGA.name: HMGA (AT-hook)
HMGA.short: HMGA1 and HMGA2 have no sequence specificity worth scanning for. They bind the minor groove of AT-rich DNA through short basic peptides called AT-hooks, which were described from the outset as recognizing DNA structure rather than base sequence, and they will bind essentially any run of A and T. The family holds three motifs, and the data show what that means: the HMGA1 models are ATTTTTA in JASPAR and TAaAATAtAtA in HOCOMOCO, the HMGA2 model is four bases at 2.2 bits, and not one of the three has another model in this family as its nearest neighbour. All three resemble models in other families more than they resemble each other. Do not treat a match here as a binding site.

CSD.name: Cold-shock domain (YBX)
CSD.short: A one-protein family. YBX1 (YB-1) carries a cold-shock domain, the eukaryotic descendant of the bacterial CspA nucleic-acid-binding fold, and it is at least as much an RNA-binding protein as a transcription factor: it packages messenger RNA, unwinds RNA secondary structure and prefers single-stranded nucleic acid over duplex DNA. Three motifs agree closely with one another - cohesion is 0.95, the highest in this part of the atlas - and all read the same eight base pairs, GATGGTAC, or its reverse complement GTACCATC. Note that this in vitro site is not the classical Y box, CTGATTGGC, with which YB-1 is historically identified; the two should not be conflated.

CG_OTHER.name: Other / unclassified
CG_OTHER.short: This is not a motif family. It is the residual category for motifs whose factor has no assigned structural family in this ontology, and in the current data it holds three matrices for three proteins. Two are the paralogous corepressors LCOR and LCORL, which carry a psq-type helix-turn-helix rather than a homeodomain and whose models are 4-5 bit A-rich strings that carry almost no information. The third is LRRFIP1, cloned as GC-binding factor 2, whose only model is a GC-rich matrix derived from ChIP-seq alone and resembles neither of the others. Internal cohesion is 0.60 and no member has a same-family neighbour that it matches. Read a hit here as unassigned rather than as shared biology, and re-report it to whichever named family the sequence actually matches.

CTCFL.name: CTCFL (BORIS)
aka: Brother of the Regulator of Imprinted Sites
CTCFL.short: CTCFL, usually called BORIS, is the single paralogue of CTCF. The two proteins share an almost identical eleven-zinc-finger array and therefore the same DNA sequence preference, so the CTCFL matrices in motif databases are simply shorter, noisier versions of the CTCF core. What differs is the protein outside the fingers and, above all, where and when it is made: CTCFL is normally confined to a narrow window of male germ-cell development, and is re-expressed in many tumors, where it is used as a cancer-testis antigen. A CTCFL motif match is a CTCF-family match; deciding which of the two proteins is bound requires expression data or an antibody, not sequence.

INSM.name: INSM1 / INSM2
INSM.short: INSM1 (originally IA-1, cloned from a human insulinoma) and its paralogue INSM2 are five-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger repressors of neuroendocrine and neuronal differentiation. Despite the family's historical placement alongside the Snail-type repressors, every matrix in this family is a GC-rich, GGGG-containing element - TGTCAGGGGGCG, or GCCCCCTGACA read on the other strand - not a CANNTG E-box. Structural work shows INSM1's fingers bind DNA with little intrinsic specificity for that element and that INSM1 reaches GGGG-containing loci largely by riding with CTCF, and TEAD1 sites through a direct TEAD1 contact. INSM1 is required for pancreatic beta cell and intestinal endocrine development and is now a standard immunohistochemical marker of neuroendocrine tumors.

ZBTB18.name: ZBTB18 (RP58)
ZBTB18.short: ZBTB18, first described as RP58, is a BTB/POZ zinc-finger repressor that binds an E-box-like site, (A/C)ACATCTG(G/T)(A/C), whose CATCTG core reads CAGATG on the opposite strand. It is a C2H2 protein, not a bHLH one, so the E-box it occupies is a site that basic helix-loop-helix activators can also use - which makes competition, not just repression, part of how it works. RP58 concentrates in condensed chromatin and represses target promoters through its POZ domain. In the brain it controls the multipolar-to-bipolar transition of newborn cortical neurons and is required for cerebellar growth; human ZBTB18 mutations cause autosomal dominant intellectual disability and figure in 1q43-q44 deletion syndrome with corpus callosum malformation.

SALL.name: SALL
SALL.short: SALL1 to SALL4 are the human Spalt-like proteins: large C2H2 zinc-finger factors built from several clusters of paired fingers, with a short N-terminal motif that recruits the NuRD corepressor complex. Their DNA binding is unusual in being defined by base composition rather than by a sequence. A single C-terminal pair of fingers in SALL4 reads AT-rich DNA, and a crystal structure shows why it is promiscuous: the contacts use small side chains in the major groove, so many different AT-rich combinations are accepted. There is consequently no reliable consensus string for this family. SALL1 mutations cause Townes-Brocks syndrome and SALL4 mutations Okihiro syndrome; SALL4 is also the cereblon substrate whose degradation explains thalidomide limb teratogenicity.

RREB1.name: RREB1
RREB1.short: RREB1 is a large C2H2 zinc-finger protein, originally identified as the factor binding the RAS-responsive element of the human calcitonin promoter in medullary thyroid carcinoma cells. It has around fifteen fingers and, in the high-throughput data that define its motif, prefers a long C-rich word usually written CCCCAAACCACCCC. It is a downstream effector of RAS and TGF-beta signalling: in the TGF-beta pathway RREB1 partners with SMAD complexes to direct fibrogenic and developmental epithelial-mesenchymal transitions, and it has been implicated in metastatic enhancer priming. The motif's length is its main virtue and its main problem, since a long C-rich element overlaps several other GC-rich promoter families and no short functional consensus has ever been agreed in the literature.

MYT1.name: MYT1 / ST18 (CCHC zinc finger)
MYT1.short: MYT1, MYT1L and ST18 are the three human members of the MYT/NZF family, which uses an unusual non-classical zinc finger (described as C2HC or CCHHC, not the C2H2 fold of most zinc-finger transcription factors) arranged in two widely separated clusters of fingers. Each cluster binds DNA independently and recognizes the same short AT-rich element, reported as AAAGTTT, and affinity rises sharply when two copies are present, so the functional element is effectively bipartite. The family matters most in neurons: MYT1L is one of the three factors that convert fibroblasts to induced neurons, where it works by repressing non-neuronal programs. MYT1L haploinsufficiency causes a human neurodevelopmental syndrome with obesity. The available motif models for this family are weak.

BZIP_OTHER.name: Other bZIP
BZIP_OTHER.short: This is not a family. It is the residual bucket in which bZIP motifs land when they do not belong to any of the defined bZIP families, and in the current data it holds exactly two entries, both from CIS-BP: a cyclic-AMP-response-element-like matrix labelled CREBL2 that was inherited from a Drosophila protein at 64 percent DNA-binding-domain identity, and a short, low-information ACGT-core matrix labelled CREBZF (Zhangfei/SMILE) taken from the mouse ortholog. The two do not resemble each other, and each is closer to a member of another family than to its bucket-mate. Read a hit here as unassigned rather than as a shared motif, and read the underlying proteins as bZIPs that act largely by partnering with, and destabilizing, other bZIPs rather than through a well-mapped element of their own.

ZBTB17.name: ZBTB17 (MIZ1)
ZBTB17.short: ZBTB17, universally called MIZ1, is a BTB/POZ protein with an unusually long array of C2H2 zinc fingers that binds core-promoter regions around transcription start sites. On its own it activates genes including the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors CDKN2B (p15INK4b) and CDKN1A (p21); when MYC binds its C-terminal helix, the same sites are converted into repressed ones, which is the main route by which MYC turns genes off. MIZ1 is therefore best understood as a promoter-anchored platform rather than as a classical enhancer-binding factor. There is no reliable in vitro sequence model for MIZ1: the two available matrices are both ChIP-derived and mutually inconsistent, one resembling a WT1-type GC/GA-rich site and the other a homeodomain ATCGAT site.

GTF3A.name: GTF3A (TFIIIA)
GTF3A.short: GTF3A encodes TFIIIA, the transcription factor in which the C2H2 zinc finger was first recognized, and the protein that made the zinc finger a general concept. It is an RNA polymerase III factor with nine fingers that binds the internal control region of 5S ribosomal RNA genes, a roughly 50-base-pair sequence inside the transcribed region rather than upstream of it, and nucleates assembly of TFIIIC and TFIIIB. TFIIIA also binds 5S rRNA itself, storing it in the 7S ribonucleoprotein particle of amphibian oocytes. Because the functional element is a long internal sequence rather than a short word, the short motifs held in databases for this factor are abstractions and should be treated with caution.

CAMTA.name: CAMTA
CAMTA.short: CAMTA1 and CAMTA2 (calmodulin-binding transcription activators) are the two human members of a family defined by the CG-1 domain, an N-terminal DNA-binding module unrelated to any other class, followed by a TIG domain, ankyrin repeats and calmodulin-binding IQ motifs. The IQ motifs make the family a direct link from calcium signaling to a DNA-binding domain. The element established for CG-1 is the plant CGCG box, (A/C/G)CGCG(G/T/C); no comparable vertebrate consensus is settled, and the two human motif models are short and only moderately consistent. CAMTA2 also acts as a coactivator recruited by NKX2-5. Loss of CAMTA1 causes ataxia in mice and congenital ataxia in humans, and a WWTR1-CAMTA1 fusion drives epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

LIN54.name: LIN54 / DREAM (CHR)
LIN54.short: LIN54 is the DNA-binding subunit of the MuvB core, the module shared by the repressive DREAM complex and the activating MMB (B-MYB-MuvB) and FOXM1-MuvB complexes. It reads a very short promoter element called the CHR, the cell cycle genes homology region, whose consensus is TTYGAA (most often TTTGAA or TTCGAA). Recognition is unusual: two tandem cysteine-rich CXC (tesmin/CRC) domains grip the duplex and two tyrosine side chains insert into the minor groove, with no zinc finger or helix-turn-helix involved. The CHR is the reason so many G2/M promoters - CCNB1, CCNB2, CDK1, CDC25C, PLK1, AURKA, UBE2C - share the same short TTYGAA, switching from repressed in G0/G1 to activated in G2/M.

CDC5L.name: CDC5L
CDC5L.short: CDC5L is the human orthologue of fission yeast Cdc5, a protein with two N-terminal Myb/SANT-like repeats whose main established job is not transcription at all: it is an essential component of the spliceosomal Prp19/CDC5L complex required for the second catalytic step of pre-mRNA splicing, and it is visible in cryo-EM structures of the human spliceosome. A site-specific DNA-binding activity was reported for the N-terminal region, and CDC5L also promotes G2/M progression and participates in the ATR-dependent S-phase checkpoint. Its motif evidence is weak: the two models in these databases disagree completely with each other, and one is inherited from an Arabidopsis protein rather than measured on human CDC5L. Treat any hit with caution.

SPZ1.name: SPZ1
SPZ1.short: SPZ1 is a single-gene family: one bHLH-Zip protein, with a basic helix-loop-helix domain followed by a leucine zipper, the same architecture as MYC, USF and the SREBPs. It was isolated from mouse testis, where expression is confined to testis and epididymis and is reduced by testosterone and retinoic acid. Unlike its palindrome-reading relatives, the one experimentally derived matrix is asymmetric, AGGGTAACAGC, from a small mouse SELEX experiment; the only other entry in the databases is a footprint archetype with a completely different, G-rich consensus. There is no ChIP-seq or in vitro human model. Overexpression studies link SPZ1 to MAPK-driven proliferation and transformation and to TWIST-mediated epithelial-mesenchymal transition in liver cancer.

CASZ1.name: CASZ1 (castor)
CASZ1.short: CASZ1 is the single human orthologue of Drosophila castor, a large multi-zinc-finger transcription factor that in flies specifies a late temporal window of neuroblast identity. The human gene sits at 1p36.22 and produces two main isoforms with different numbers of C2H2 zinc fingers. Its binding preference is poorly characterized: the only motif in these databases is a long, AT-rich composite model from in vitro selection, and no consensus has been established by focused biochemistry. CASZ1 is required for cardiac and vascular morphogenesis in Xenopus and mouse, its expression is low in high-risk neuroblastoma where 1p36 is frequently deleted, and common variants at the CASZ1 locus are among the earliest replicated blood-pressure associations.

CIC.name: CIC (capicua)
CIC.short: CIC (capicua) is a single HMG-box repressor and the transcriptional sensor of ERK/MAPK signaling. It binds an eight-base octamer, TGAATGAA or TCAATGAA, and recruits Groucho/TLE and SIN3-histone deacetylase complexes to switch target genes off; MAPK activity removes CIC from those sites and lets them fire. Unusually for an HMG-box protein, the HMG box alone cannot bind DNA - a distant C-terminal motif called C1 is required with it, and the two together form a bipartite recognition surface. CIC is inactivated in most IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendrogliomas, with mutations clustering in the C1 domain, and the CIC-DUX4 fusion defines a subset of undifferentiated round cell sarcoma. Its main direct targets are the PEA3/ETS genes ETV1, ETV4 and ETV5.

HBP1.name: HBP1
HBP1.short: HBP1 is a single HMG-box transcriptional repressor and cell-cycle inhibitor, identified as a target of the retinoblastoma protein family. Its highest-affinity site, found in the human CD2 locus control region, is the twelve-base element TTCATTCATTCA, which is explicitly not the canonical HMG-box consensus used by SOX and TCF/LEF proteins; read on the other strand it is three tandem copies of TGAATGAA, the octamer that CIC recognizes. HBP1 represses the N-MYC and cyclin D1 promoters, opposes E2F at N-MYC, activates p16 and p21, and arrests the cell cycle even under strong growth signals. It is suppressed by AKT signaling and by several microRNAs, and behaves as a tumor suppressor without being a commonly mutated cancer gene.

PUR.name: PURA / PURB
PUR.short: PURA and PURB (Pur-alpha and Pur-beta) are PUR-repeat proteins that bind purine-rich DNA and RNA, with a strong preference for single strands rather than duplex. The PUR element was defined as a repeated purine-rich sequence upstream of the human c-MYC P1 promoter, at a site of DNA bending inside a replication initiation zone, and was given the consensus GGNNGAGGGAGARRRR. The PUR repeats fold into a Whirly-like domain, and Pur-alpha can unwind double-stranded DNA rather than simply read it. These proteins act mostly as repressors, best characterized on the smooth muscle alpha-actin promoter, where they bind the GGN-repeat strand of core enhancer elements. De novo PURA variants cause PURA syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder with neonatal hypotonia, seizures and severe developmental delay.
